Askeladden ror over vannet med de sju sølvendene til trollet.

Alt: Askeladden sitter i et stort trau av tre midt på vannet med sju blanke sølvender rundt seg. Langt bak ham lener trollet seg ut av fjellet og rister på neven.

Askeladden sits in his big wooden kneading trough in the middle of the calm lake, paddling towards the viewer with a cheeky grin, the seven silver ducks riding in the trough around him. Far behind him the Troll leans out of the dark crack in the Grey Mountain and shakes his fist. The water glitters in golden evening light.

Full prompt
Create a square, full-bleed children's storybook cover illustration, no title or text. Warm Scandinavian gouache and watercolour on cream textured paper, soft coloured-pencil outlines, visible handmade brushwork, rounded friendly shapes, cosy magical mood. Late-summer golden evening at a blue mountain lake in old rural Norway. Askeladden sits in a broad shallow oval bread-kneading trough carved from solid wood, paddling toward the viewer with one short wooden paddle and a cheeky grin. Exactly seven polished silver ducks sit around him inside the trough: three to his left and four to his right, each head clearly visible. The trough has blunt rounded ends and thick rough edges; no pointed boat bow, planks or benches. Far behind him across the lake, a huge rounded grey granite mountain rises at the opposite shore. The Troll leans from a dark door-shaped crack in that mountain, comically grumpy and shaking one fist. Keep the Troll small in the distant composition; no threat or harm. Birch trees and mossy boulders line the mountain's narrow pebble beach. Lingonberry red is the recurring accent, warm cream highlights, honey-yellow light, forest green, fjord-blue water. Image 1 is Askeladden's character sheet; match his straw-blond messy hair, red knitted cap, blue-grey eyes, freckles, ash-smudged cheek, patched linen shirt, short brown waistcoat, grey-brown breeches. Draw him once. Image 2 is the Troll's sheet; match his round belly, lumpy mossy grey-green skin, long knobbly nose, two stubby teeth, floppy ears, dry-grass beard, spruce sapling on his head, ragged brown tunic and rope belt. Draw him once. Single clear scene, no borders, no lettering, no extra characters, no photorealism or glossy 3D.

Use case: illustration-story. Square format, 1024 × 1024.

Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste broren, snill og oppfinnsom, som aldri gir opp og bruker hodet i stedet for kreftene.

A lanky, cheerful Norwegian farm boy of about fourteen with messy straw-blond hair, big blue-grey eyes, a small snub nose, freckles and a smudge of ash on one cheek. He wears a faded red knitted cap, a patched undyed linen shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a short brown wool waistcoat, grey-brown knee breeches, grey wool socks and worn brown leather shoes.

Den eldste broren eldste-bror · the Eldest Brother

Den eldste broren, stor i kjeften og lat, som heller sover i høyet enn å stelle hestene.

A tall, broad-shouldered young man of about twenty with a square jaw, a smug grin, short dark-brown hair and a thin moustache. He wears a dark-green wool jacket over a white shirt, brown breeches and tall black boots.

Den mellomste broren mellomste-bror · the Middle Brother

Den mellomste broren, som skulle stelle hagen, men helst surmuler når andre får skryt.

A plump young man of about eighteen with round red cheeks, a sulky pout and curly ginger hair. He wears a mustard-yellow wool tunic with a rope belt, patched brown trousers and wooden clogs.

Kongen kongen · the King

En rettferdig konge som elsker vakre ting og holder ord når Askeladden lykkes.

A kindly, round-bellied old king with a long, soft white beard, rosy cheeks and small round spectacles. He wears a small gold crown, a long red robe with white fur trim and gold embroidery, and soft red slippers.

Trollet i fjellet trollet · the Troll

Et stort troll som bor inne i fjellet, brøler mye og blir til slutt så sint at han sprekker som en ballong.

An enormous, round-bellied troll three times as tall as a man, with grey-green lumpy skin patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide grumpy mouth with two stubby teeth, big floppy ears, a tangled beard like dry grass and a small spruce sapling growing on top of his head. He wears a ragged brown hide tunic tied with rope and goes barefoot on huge flat feet.

Trolldatteren trolldatteren · the Troll's Daughter

Trollets store datter, lett å lure når Askeladden prater rolig og smart.

A huge troll girl, about three times as tall as Askeladden, with a round moss-green face, a long bumpy nose, small squinting eyes, pink cheeks and one enormous reddish-brown braid so long that it trails on the floor behind her. She wears a patched grey wool dress with a big faded red shawl over her shoulders and goes barefoot.

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste sønnen, rolig og smart, som møter utfordringer med oppfinnsomhet og en vennlig selvsikkerhet.

A small, wiry boy of about eleven, shorter than most boys his age, with a round face, rosy cheeks, bright brown eyes, a button nose, a dark-brown curly mop of hair and a cheeky gap-toothed grin. He wears a moss-green knitted jumper with brown leather elbow patches, dark-brown knee breeches, thick oatmeal-coloured wool stockings and scuffed brown boots. A small brown linen sack with a drawstring hangs from his shoulder.

Trollet trollet · the Troll

Skogens store vokter som først virker streng, men lar seg lett imponere og blir mer komisk enn farlig.

A giant forest troll, so tall that his head pokes up among the treetops, with cracked, bark-brown skin like an old pine trunk, a shaggy black haystack of hair full of twigs and dry leaves, a potato nose, small twinkly yellow eyes, an enormous mouth that stretches from ear to ear with big square teeth, long dangling arms and a huge, round belly. He wears baggy, patched sackcloth trousers held up by braces of twisted roots, and no shirt.

Faren faren · the Father

En gammel og sliten bonde som ønsker at sønnene skal arbeide så familien kan klare seg bedre.

A short, stocky, bow-legged old farmer of about seventy with a broad, weather-beaten, wrinkled face, a big bulbous nose, small twinkling eyes under shaggy grey eyebrows and a thick, bristly grey beard cut short and square. He wears a battered, wide-brimmed black felt hat, a patched grey-blue wool jacket with horn buttons over a collarless linen shirt, brown knee breeches with braces, grey wool stockings and wooden clogs.

Den eldste broren eldste-bror · the Eldest Brother

Askeladdens eldste bror, stor og sterk, men så redd for trollet at øksa glipper og han springer hjem.

A hulking, broad-shouldered young man of about nineteen with a thick neck, a broad, flat face, a crooked nose, small pale-blue eyes, heavy black eyebrows and short, bristly black hair cropped close to his head. He wears a shaggy, sleeveless sheepskin vest over a rough grey homespun shirt, baggy brown trousers tied under the knees with leather laces, and heavy black boots.

Den mellomste broren mellomste-bror · the Middle Brother

Askeladdens mellomste bror, som springer så fort fra trollet at lua blir hengende igjen på en grein.

A thin, jittery young man of about sixteen with a long neck, a narrow face, a long pointed nose, big worried eyes and frizzy light-brown hair. On his head sits a long, floppy, bright-yellow knitted stocking cap with a blue tassel. He wears a baggy blue linen smock belted with a cord, patched grey trousers and wooden clogs.

The hunter is a kind man out for a stroll: he carries only his walking stick and a leather game bag. The dunlin and her chicks are natural birds.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Fox: A slim, light-footed, long-legged red fox with sleek, bright flame-red fur, a snow-white chin, throat and chest, black lower legs and paws, tall pointed ears with black backs, narrow amber eyes with a sly sideways glance, a long, pointed snout with long whiskers and a cheeky lopsided grin. His big, bushy red tail ends in a clean white tip.
- the Bear: A huge, heavy, slow-moving bear, taller than a man when he stands up, with thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, and a patient, slightly puzzled look. He has enormous flat paws with blunt claws and, unlike bears today, a long, fine, plume-like bushy tail that reaches the ground and sweeps the snow behind him.

Setting:
- the Frozen Lake: A small, round forest lake frozen solid, its thick ice pale grey-blue and dusted with snow, ringed by tall, snow-laden spruces and a few bare birches. Snowy reeds poke up along the shore, round boulders wear caps of snow, the shore is a soft, deep snowbank, and gentle white hills rise beyond.

Story world: A snowy forest in old Norway, long ago, where the animals can talk. Below the spruce woods lies the Frozen Lake, a small forest lake covered with thick, snow-dusted ice. Up the hill is the Sunny Slope, an open clearing where the low winter sun shines, with one dense, dark spruce bush at its upper edge. The fox's bundle of fish is five plump silver fish tied together by their tails with a piece of string. The butter tub is a small, round wooden keg with a flat lid and two bent-wood hoops, about as tall as the fox, full of bright-yellow butter. The bear and the fox are natural wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

This story's season, light and colours: Deep midwinter in bright, dazzling sunshine: sparkling white snow, a clear turquoise-blue sky, cool blue shadows and hoarfrost glittering on every twig, with the frozen lake a pale grey-blue. Near Christmas the Sunny Slope basks in warm lemon-yellow sunshine, and the last picture is a clear, deep-blue evening with a lemon glow low in the sky and the first stars. Accents: the fox's flame red, butter yellow and dark spruce green.

Bjørnen bjorn · the Bear

Stor og sterk, men litt lett å lure; han vil gjerne lære og gjøre det rette, selv når det går litt galt.

A huge, heavy, slow-moving bear, taller than a man when he stands up, with thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, and a patient, slightly puzzled look. He has enormous flat paws with blunt claws and, unlike bears today, a long, fine, plume-like bushy tail that reaches the ground and sweeps the snow behind him.

Den stubbrumpete bjørnen bjorn-stubbrumpet · the Stub-tailed Bear

Den samme snille bjørnen etter isfisket, nå med bare en liten halestump igjen; han blir aldri sint lenge og stoler fortsatt på reven.

The same huge, heavy, slow-moving bear after his fishing trip: thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, a patient, slightly puzzled look and enormous flat paws with blunt claws. His long tail is gone: all that is left is a tiny, round, fluffy stump on his big round bottom.

Reven rev · the Fox

Smart og rampete, mer ertende enn slem; han liker å finne på små triks og gliser når han lykkes.

A slim, light-footed, long-legged red fox with sleek, bright flame-red fur, a snow-white chin, throat and chest, black lower legs and paws, tall pointed ears with black backs, narrow amber eyes with a sly sideways glance, a long, pointed snout with long whiskers and a cheeky lopsided grin. Story world: Old rural Norway in early summer, long ago. The king's castle is a large palace of dark logs with grass-covered turf roofs, carved dragon gables and a wide courtyard, among blooming meadows. In a meadow by the road stands the grassy tussock where the tiny maiden lives: a round, knee-high hump of grass and clover that opens like a little door. Inside is a snug, round room with walls of woven roots, a tiny chair, a tiny spinning wheel and a tiny loom. The tiny shirt is snow-white linen with perfect little stitches, no bigger than a man's palm. Her carriage is an ordinary shiny silver tablespoon pulled by two small white mice with reins of red thread. The big lake by the road is wide and still, with reeds and water lilies. Askeladden's horse is a sturdy dun fjord horse with a black-and-cream striped mane.

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste prinsen, som brødrene ikke vil ha med, men som møter verden med godt hjerte og mot.

A tall, gangly young prince of about seventeen with long arms and legs, a long face with deep dimples when he smiles, warm hazel eyes, a straight nose and copper-red hair cut in a round bowl cut. He wears a sky-blue linen smock under a shiny steel breastplate that is a little too big for him, a brown leather belt, loose grey trousers and tall brown riding boots.

Dukken i gresset dukken-i-graesset · the Tiny Grass Maiden

En fin og vennlig jente, først ikke større enn en dukke, som syr en skjorte på én dag og blir like stor som Askeladden etter at hun faller i vannet.

A doll-sized young woman of about seventeen, no taller than a doll, slim and light on her feet, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a bright smile. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long pigtails tied with grass-green ribbons, with little daisies and buttercups tucked into it. She wears a simple ankle-length white linen dress with a narrow grass-green sash and tiny green slippers.

Dukken i gresset (stor) dukken-i-graesset-stor · the Grass Maiden

Dukken i gresset etter at havmannen har hentet henne opp av vannet: nå like stor som Askeladden, og enda finere enn før.

A full-sized young woman of about seventeen, slim and graceful, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a bright smile. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long pigtails tied with grass-green ribbons, under a wreath of daisies and buttercups. She wears a finer ankle-length white linen dress embroidered with little green leaves and white flowers along the hem and sleeves, a grass-green sash and green slippers.

Kongen kongen · the King

Faren som setter prøven, men som kjenner igjen flinkhet og godhet når han ser det.

A tall, thin, elderly king with narrow, sloping shoulders, a long, lined face, a long pointed nose, shrewd grey eyes under thin arched eyebrows and a neat, pointed grey goatee. He wears a tall, pointed golden crown, a long deep-blue robe with a wide border of rosemaling flowers in red, white and yellow, and pointed dark-blue shoes.

Havmannen havmanden · the Merman

Et vennlig vesen med fiskehale som bærer Dukken i gresset opp av vannet. Da er hun ikke liten lenger.

A big, friendly merman, a man from the waist up and a fish from the waist down, with a broad, weathered, kind face, a wide flat nose, twinkling sea-green eyes and a gentle smile. His long, wet, dark-green hair hangs to his waist with strands of pondweed in it, and he has a short, curly beard of the same green and a necklace of white river shells. His long tail is covered in shiny silver scales with a blue-green shimmer and ends in a wide, fan-shaped fin.

In a meadow by the road stands the grassy tussock where the tiny maiden lives: a round, knee-high hump of grass and clover that opens like a little door. Inside is a snug, round room with walls of woven roots, a tiny chair, a tiny spinning wheel and a tiny loom. The tiny shirt is snow-white linen with perfect little stitches, no bigger than a man's palm. Her carriage is an ordinary shiny silver tablespoon pulled by two small white mice with reins of red thread. The big lake by the road is wide and still, with reeds and water lilies. Askeladden's horse is a sturdy dun fjord horse with a black-and-cream striped mane.

This story's season, light and colours: Early summer: meadows full of buttercups, cornflowers, clover and white daisies, fresh bright-green grass sparkling with dew, and clear morning light under a pale-blue sky with small white clouds. The lake is silver-blue and still. At the castle, a passing summer shower leaves puddles and everything glistening wet.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Den svarte hesten slik han egentlig er: en ung prins som ble trollet om til hest. Nå er han fri, og han og den unge kongen blir gode venner.

He wears a charcoal-black riding coat with silver frogging across the chest, a silver-grey cloak fastened with a silver horseshoe-shaped brooch, black breeches and tall black riding boots.

Den fremmede mannen den-fremmede-mannen · the Stranger

En streng og farlig herre som setter forbud og prøver å skremme gutten, men som til slutt mister makten når gutten får hjelp til å slippe unna.

An unusually tall, gaunt figure who almost looks like a man: a long, craggy face with a stony grey complexion, a huge knobbly nose, small glinting black eyes under bushy iron-grey eyebrows, a wide thin mouth, big pointed ears and a short, bristly iron-grey beard. He has very long arms, huge knobbly hands and enormous flat feet in big black boots, and he wears a long black frock coat that reaches his ankles, buttoned with large horn buttons, and a tall, battered black hat.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

En modig og snill prinsesse som ser godheten i gutten og står opp for ham, og som gleder seg over at han hjelper riket.

A warm, spirited princess of about seventeen with a round face, a small straight nose, bright hazel eyes, dimples and fair skin with rosy cheeks. Her dark-brown hair hangs in two long, thick braids tied with pink ribbons. She wears a rose-pink linen dress with puffed sleeves, a white embroidered collar and a darker pink sash, soft pink shoes, and a thin silver circlet set with a small pink stone.

Kongen kongen · the King

En streng, men rettferdig konge. Først blir han sint på gutten, men senere forstår han sannheten og belønner mot og godhet.

A broad, barrel-chested, middle-aged king with a square, stern face, a big hooked nose, deep-set dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows, and a thick, bushy black beard streaked with grey. He wears a heavy crown of dark iron topped with gold points, a long dark-green velvet robe with gold trim, a broad brown leather belt with a big gold buckle and tall black riding boots.

The rope hangs loose from the iron ring, and a trail of wet footprints leads across the plank floor.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The widow lives in a tiny grey log cottage with a sagging turf roof. The Stranger's house stands alone in a dark spruce forest: a tall, gloomy house of smoke-blackened logs, whose long hallway has four identical closed plank doors painted dark oxblood red, with black iron ring handles. The thorn whip is a small bundle of thorny dog-rose twigs, the stone is round, grey and as big as a loaf, the water jar is a small brown clay jar with a cork, and the ointment sits in a tiny round blue clay pot. The copper cauldron is huge, round and gleaming. The hollow linden stands alone on a green meadow in the forest. The king's farm has big turf-roofed log halls and a round grey stone tower. The king's handkerchief is fine white linen with a small gold crown embroidered in one corner.

This story's season, light and colours: High summer in full bloom: emerald-green meadows and gardens heavy with pink wild roses and creamy elderflower, and bright, clear days under tall white clouds. Inside the Stranger's house: dim candlelight, dark smoky timber and the warm glow of copper. Accent colours: wild-rose pink, emerald green and gleaming copper.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:

The copper cauldron is huge, round and gleaming. The hollow linden stands alone on a green meadow in the forest. The king's farm has big turf-roofed log halls and a round grey stone tower. The king's handkerchief is fine white linen with a small gold crown embroidered in one corner.

This story's season, light and colours: High summer in full bloom: emerald-green meadows and gardens heavy with pink wild roses and creamy elderflower, and bright, clear days under tall white clouds. Inside the Stranger's house: dim candlelight, dark smoky timber and the warm glow of copper. Accent colours: wild-rose pink, emerald green and gleaming copper.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in late winter. The poor little farm is a single tiny, lopsided cottage of grey, weathered logs with a sagging, snow-covered turf roof, a crooked chimney, one small window and a low door. Inside is one cramped room with a bare plank floor, a rough little table, a wobbly bench along the wall, two rickety stools and a three-legged stool, a small stone fireplace in the corner with a sooty kettle, and one shelf with two cracked clay bowls. Almost everything is old, grey and patched. The only new things in the house are the farmer's one new sleeve, the wife's one new shoe and the daughter's new cap. The suitor carries a small, square brown leather travel bag with a brass clasp.

This story's season, light and colours: Late winter on a frosty February afternoon: old, crusted snow with lilac-blue shadows, long icicles on the eaves and a low, pink sun. Inside the cottage: warm orange firelight and smoky brown shadows, from which the family's three new things shine out: a bright lingonberry-red sleeve, a glossy black shoe with a silver buckle and an emerald-green cap.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Youngest Prince: A slim, brave young prince of about eighteen with a kind, open face, a straight nose, steady green-grey eyes, a quick smile and wavy dark-brown hair falling to his shoulders. He wears a forest-green hunting jacket with brass buttons and a high collar over a white shirt, a brown leather belt, dark-grey trousers and tall brown boots, with a small gold brooch shaped like a ship pinned to his collar.
- the Giant Bird: An enormous, friendly bird as tall as a three-storey house, so big that a man reaches only to its ankle, shaped a little like a giant gull. It has a pale silver-grey back, broad silver-grey wings with black tips, a snowy-white head and breast, kind dark eyes, a big hooked golden-yellow beak and huge orange feet. From the back of its neck rises one enormous, stiff, copper-red feather, as thick as a small spruce tree.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea, long ago, over fourteen years of voyages. The princesses' father rules a royal farm of big log halls above a sandy beach. On a small rocky island stands the troll prince's castle; far across the sea, a dark stone castle on a rocky shore holds the troll king's great hall of gold. The little dog is fluffy and white, with floppy brown ears. The old sword has a plain iron hilt; the magic bottle is round and made of blue glass. The crown cupboard is waist-high, painted blue with red-and-white rosemaling, and holds twelve small golden crowns. The iron boat is small, dark and has no oars, with a heavy iron club inside. The eleven older princes wear matching grey-blue coats; the eleven older princesses wear long dresses in different soft colours.

This story's season, light and colours: Changeable weather on the open northern sea in spring, from gales to calm, bright days: jade-green and pewter-grey waves with white foam, towering silver-grey clouds and clear rosy dawns. Indoors, warm lamplight and the rich glow of polished gold. Accents: Ridder Rød's scarlet, the prince's forest green and gleaming golden crowns.

Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.

Characters

Den yngste kongssønnen den-yngste-kongssonnen · the Youngest Prince

Den yngste av tolv brødre, som holder seg våken når alle andre sover, redder prinsessene og kommer tilbake forkledd som sjømann.

A slim, brave young prince of about eighteen with a kind, open face, a straight nose, steady green-grey eyes, a quick smile and wavy dark-brown hair falling to his shoulders. He wears a forest-green hunting jacket with brass buttons and a high collar over a white shirt, a brown leather belt, dark-grey trousers and tall brown boots, with a small gold brooch shaped like a ship pinned to his collar.

Den yngste kongssønnen som sjømann sjomannen · the Sailor

Den yngste kongssønnen i forkledning, med en stor sjømannsjakke og et rødt tørkle rundt hodet. Først later han som han er en stakkars sjømann, og så en kremmer.

A slim young man of about eighteen disguised as a poor sailor, with a kind face, a straight nose, steady green-grey eyes and a few days' dark stubble. His wavy dark-brown hair is tucked under a red kerchief knotted around his head. He wears a huge, baggy, dark-blue knitted sailor's jacket with wooden buttons that hangs down to his knees, patched canvas trousers and scuffed, salt-stained boots.

Den yngste prinsessen den-yngste-prinsessen · the Youngest Princess

Den yngste av de tolv, stille men modig, som beskytter seg selv og til slutt tør å si sannheten.

A small, slender princess of about seventeen with a round, solemn face, a short nose, dark-blue eyes under thick, level brows and a small, determined mouth. Her honey-brown hair is braided into a crown around her head. She wears a long cream-coloured dress with gold embroidery on the bodice and hem, long fitted sleeves and a narrow gold belt, with a tiny silver brooch shaped like an anchor at her throat.

Fugl Dam fugl-dam · the Giant Bird

En enorm, hjelpsom fugl som hjelper kongssønnen når han blir forlatt, og flyr ham trygt dit han trenger å være.

An enormous, friendly bird as tall as a three-storey house, so big that a man reaches only to its ankle, shaped a little like a giant gull. It has a pale silver-grey back, broad silver-grey wings with black tips, a snowy-white head and breast, kind dark eyes, a big hooked golden-yellow beak and huge orange feet. From the back of its neck rises one enormous, stiff, copper-red feather, as thick as a small spruce tree.

Ridder Rød ridder-rod · Ridder Rød

Styrmannen som blir misunnelig og prøver å ta æren, men som til slutt mister makten når sannheten kommer fram.

A tall, barrel-chested, vain knight of about forty with a big square jaw, a cleft chin, a short straight nose held high, small, cold pale-blue eyes and a proud smirk. He has short flame-red hair and a short, pointed flame-red beard. He wears a round, polished steel helmet with a stiff red crest, a long scarlet surcoat with a gold border over a shirt of shiny chainmail, a wide black belt with a big gold buckle and tall black boots.

Trollkongen med tolv hoder trollkongen · the Troll King

En trollkonge med tolv snorkende hoder som prinsessene må klø dagen lang, helt til han blir til tåke, ett hode om gangen.

A huge, hulking troll about three times as tall as a man, with rust-red, warty skin, a broad, sagging barrel of a body, very long arms that hang down to the floor and short bowed legs. On top of his thick neck sits a bunch of exactly twelve small heads, packed tightly together like a bunch of turnips, each with a knobbly nose, droopy ears and a wispy tuft of pale straw-coloured hair. He wears a moth-eaten dark-blue velvet cloak with a tattered fur collar.

Trollprinsen trollprinsen · the Troll Prince

Et stort, rart og ganske greit troll som gir kongssønnen sverdet og flasken, og som blir konge når trollkongen er borte.

A huge, strange troll about three times as tall as a man, shaped like a giant sack of flour, with sloping shoulders, a small head, a big soft belly, short legs and huge webbed feet like a duck's. His skin is a weathered, ruddy tan. He has a nose as long as a cucumber, small kind amber eyes, big ears like cabbage leaves and a stiff crest of dark-brown hair standing straight up like a brush. He wears a mulberry-purple velvet tunic with a wide gold belt.

Trollprinsens datter trollprinsens-datter · the Troll Prince's Daughter

Trollprinsens datter. Først er hun en liten hund som bjeffer på en øy, så blir hun til en prinsesse med langt, lyst hår og et tynt slør som svever rundt henne.

A willowy young woman of about eighteen with pale, milky skin, a long, narrow face, a tiny pointed nose, big silvery-grey eyes and long, pale-blonde hair that floats and drifts around her as if she were under water. A thin, misty veil floats around her too, as if lifted by a breeze. She wears a long, flowing apricot-coloured dress with a silver belt and goes barefoot.

Kongen kongen · the King

Kongen som har tolv døtre og er så glad i dem at han vil ha dem hos seg hele tiden.

A small, wiry, elderly king with a narrow, kind, crinkly face, a small sharp nose, twinkling blue eyes, wisps of silver hair poking out under his crown and a long silver-grey beard braided into two plaits tied with little gold rings. He wears a low, wide gold crown set with green stones, a long turquoise robe with a collar of spotted grey sealskin and silver clasps shaped like fish, and soft grey felt slippers.

Den nysgjerrige konen den-nysgjerrige-konen · the Nosy Old Woman

Den mest nysgjerrige konen i hele landet. Hun spør og spør, og løper rett til venninnene sine med nyheten.

A short, bustling old woman with a plump little body on thin legs, like a robin, and a long neck that she cranes forward to see everything. She has a sharp little chin, a beaky nose, big curious eyes magnified by thick, round bottle-bottom spectacles and wispy white hair scraped into a tiny topknot like an onion. She wears a faded lavender dress, an orange knitted shawl and a patched brown apron with a deep pocket.

The widower's little red farmhouse has a low kitchen with a plank table, and next to it grows a field of tall, bushy green hemp. Beyond the village lies a big, dark spruce forest. The farms have sheep barns, goose houses and, at the rich farmer's, a stabbur: a dark timber storehouse on stilts, hung inside with sausages and hams and with shelves of round loaves. On Sunday morning everything happens at the Turnip Field above the bog. Giske's soot is black and sticky, made of tallow and chimney soot.

The three raids happen on dark, starry nights lit only by a thin moon and one warm lantern, and Sunday morning is fresh and dewy, with pearl-grey mist over the brown bog. Accent colours: sooty black, turnip purple and Giske's plum.

Giske giske · Giske

Sterk og flink hushjelp med lange bein som blir smurt svart med talg og sot mens hun sover, tror hun er et troll og hjelper to tyver altfor høylytt.

A very tall, strong woman of about thirty with the longest legs in the village, a head taller than any man, long arms and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, rosy weathered cheeks, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun on top of her head. She wears a knee-length plum-purple wool dress with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a cream apron and a ring of big iron keys on her belt.

Giske som troll giske-sotete · Sooty Giske

Giske smurt svart med talg og sot på armer, bein og nese, så hun tror hun er blitt et troll. Beina er like lange som før, og stemmen er høyere enn noensinne.

Giske after the widower's trick: the same very tall, strong woman with the longest legs in the village, a long oval face, hazel eyes, a wide mouth and flaxen hair in a tall bun on top of her head. Her arms and long bare legs are smeared completely black with sticky soot, her cheeks are smudged, and a big round black blob sits on the tip of her nose. Her knee-length plum-purple dress and cream apron are streaked with black, and a ring of big iron keys hangs on her belt.

Enkemannen enkemannen · the Widower

Enkemannen Giske steller hus for, så lei av masingen hennes at han smører henne inn med sot mens hun sover.

A skinny, stooped widower of about fifty with a long, narrow, tired face, heavy-lidded eyes, a long crooked nose, hollow cheeks, a scruffy salt-and-pepper chin beard and thin dark hair combed flat. He wears a collarless off-white shirt, dark-blue braces, baggy grey trousers, a darned heather-brown knitted cardigan and worn leather slippers, and he always looks as if he longs for some peace and quiet.

Den tynne tyven tyven-tynn · the Skinny Thief

Den ene av de to sultne tyvene som tar med seg Giske fordi hun vet hvor sauene bor. Han er tynn og skvetten og hysjer mest av alle.

A skinny, jittery thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black knitted hat. He wears a patched charcoal jacket that is too short in the arms, grey striped trousers and worn-out shoes, and carries an empty flour sack under his arm.

Den tykke tyven tyven-tykk · the Plump Thief

Den andre av de to sultne tyvene. Han er liten og rund, og magen hans rumler så fælt at han gjerne vil ha med seg et troll når de skal ut og stjele.

A short, round, nervous thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a brown flat cap. He wears a tight mustard-brown waistcoat with one button missing over a grey shirt, baggy trousers held up with rope and big boots, and carries a coil of rope over his shoulder.

Bonden bonden · the Farmer

Bonden som våkner av bråket, kommer ut med lykta og blir livredd for trollet som herjer på gårdene.

A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a bony, hollow-cheeked face, a hooked nose, bristly grey stubble, startled round eyes and wild, tousled grey hair, just woken up. He wears only a long, loose, undyed linen nightshirt that reaches his knees, with bare skinny legs and bare feet, and holds up a small tin lantern with a warm, flickering candle inside.

Bonden med nepeåkeren nepebonden · the Turnip Farmer

Bonden som eier nepeåkeren. Han ser trollet midt i nepene sine, lokker presten ut av senga med en kalvestek og bærer ham over myra på ryggen.

A short, sturdy, bow-legged farmer of about fifty with a square, weather-beaten face, a big bristly chestnut moustache, round startled eyes, bushy eyebrows and wiry grey hair that sticks up under a wide, frayed straw hat. He wears a faded rust-orange wool vest over a white shirt with rolled sleeves, green knee breeches, long grey socks and wooden clogs.

Presten presten · the Priest

Søvnig prest i nattlue og tøfler som blir lokket ut av senga med en kalvestek og havner midt i myra.

A very round, heavy priest of about sixty-five with a big belly, short legs, a pink, jowly, clean-shaven face, puffy sleepy eyes, bushy white eyebrows and a fringe of white curls poking out under a long red-and-white striped nightcap with a tassel. He wears only his long, crumpled white nightshirt reaching his ankles and a pair of fluffy blue felt slippers.

En vennlig vandrer som ber høflig om en liten smakebit og minner om at det er godt å dele.

A very old, tall and slightly stooped wanderer with a long, gentle face, deep-set kind blue-grey eyes, a high wrinkled forehead, thin snow-white hair to his shoulders and a long, flowing white beard that reaches his belt. He wears a plain, ankle-length hooded brown homespun robe tied with a rope, and simple sandals over woollen foot-wraps. He leans on a tall, knobbly wooden staff. A humble traveller with no halo.

Sankt Peder sankt-peder · St Peter

En trofast følgesvenn på vandringen som står ved siden av og følger med.

A short, sturdy, round-shouldered old man of about sixty-five with a round, cheerful face, a shiny bald head with a fringe of short grey hair around the back, big ears, a broad flat nose, bright brown eyes and a short, bristly grey beard. He wears a knee-length faded green tunic with a leather belt, brown woollen leggings, a short brown hooded cape and worn leather boots. A small bronze key hangs from his belt. No halo.

Gjertrudsfuglen gjertrudsfuglen · the Red-Capped Bird

Den lille fuglen Gjertrud blir til, mørk av sot men fortsatt med en rød lue, som leter etter mat i trær og gleder seg til regn.

A small black woodpecker, sooty black all over from beak to tail with slightly ruffled, soot-smudged feathers, and on top of its head a bright scarlet crest shaped exactly like a tiny pointed stocking cap with a tassel. It has a strong, pointed ivory-white beak, round pale-yellow eyes with a slightly grumpy look, stiff black tail feathers for propping itself against tree trunks and grey clawed feet for clinging to bark.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in the days when Our Lord and St Peter wandered the earth. Gjertrud's home is a small, low log cottage with a thick snow-covered turf roof and a squat grey stone chimney, alone at the edge of a snowy spruce forest. Inside is one warm, firelit room: an open stone hearth with a big, round, flat iron griddle over the embers, a long wooden baking board dusted with flour, a rolling pin, a wooden bench by the door, and a tall stack of lefser, which are big, thin, round, soft flatbreads, pale with brown speckles. Every lefse she rolls, however tiny the lump of dough, grows on the griddle until it is far too big.

This story's season, light and colours: A hushed early-winter evening in the blue hour: big, soft snowflakes drifting down, thick snow on roofs and spruces, and everything outside in deep, velvety blues. Inside the cottage: warm amber firelight, golden-brown lefser and pale flour. The bright scarlet of the red cap is the one strong accent colour, later joined by the bird's sooty black.

The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Gudbrand and his wife have three small children: a boy of about eight with short black hair and a green jumper, a girl of about six with two stubby fair plaits and a red dress, and a chubby toddler in a long white shirt. Accents: the Wife's cornflower-blue apron and bright red rowan berries.

Alt: Døra står åpen, og varmt lys strømmer ut i snøen. Naboen står bøyd med hånda bak øret og smiler flaut, mens Gudbrand holder døra og kona vinker ham inn til bordet.

Seen from the snowy yard of the Hillside Farm on a starry night: the dusky-blue cottage door stands wide open and warm light pours out onto the snow. On the doorstep, the Neighbour, still bent over with one mitten cupped behind his ear, grins sheepishly. Gudbrand holds the door open, smiling broadly around his pipe. Inside, the Wife waves the Neighbour in towards the supper table, where the three children are already sitting.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Seen from the snowy yard of the Hillside Farm on a starry night: the dusky-blue cottage door stands wide open and warm light pours out onto the snow. On the doorstep, the Neighbour, still bent over with one mitten cupped behind his ear, grins sheepishly. Gudbrand holds the door open, smiling broadly around his pipe. Inside, the Wife waves the Neighbour in towards the supper table, where the three children are already sitting.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Gudbrand: A short, round, easy-going old farmer of about seventy with a round belly, a shiny bald head, fluffy white side-whiskers from his ears down to his jaw, a clean-shaven chin, a big pink nose, small merry blue eyes and a calm, contented smile. He wears a soft dark-green felt hat with a narrow brim, a thick knitted jacket with a black-and-white snowflake pattern and pewter clasps, a red knitted scarf, brown breeches, grey wool stockings and heavy boots, and always has a short curved wooden pipe.
- the Wife: A plump, cheerful farm wife of about sixty-five, a little shorter than Gudbrand, with a round, beaming face, rosy cheeks, a broad, freckled nose, merry hazel eyes that crinkle when she laughs, and grey hair pinned up in a neat bun. She wears a long rose-red wool dress with a white linen collar and rolled-up sleeves, a bright cornflower-blue apron with a big bow at the back, and a cream knitted shawl round her shoulders.
- the Neighbour: A nosy, pot-bellied farmer of about fifty with a round, clean-shaven face, a long, pointed, twitchy nose, narrow doubtful eyes with one eyebrow always raised, big pink ears that stick straight out and short, spiky ginger hair. He wears a thick, knee-length sheepskin coat with the fleece showing at the collar and cuffs, a round brown fur hat with its ear flaps tied up on top, brown mittens and tall grey felt boots.

Setting:
- the Hillside Farm: A tiny farm high on a steep, snowy hillside: a low, dark-brown log cottage with a thick, snow-covered turf roof, a stone chimney, two small four-paned windows and a sturdy plank door painted dusky blue, with a little cowshed beside it. A birch and a rowan tree with red berries stand in the yard next to a sheaf of oats on a tall pole, and a narrow path zigzags steeply down towards the valley far below.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in a deep mountain valley in the week before Christmas. Gudbrand's small farm sits high up on a steep hillside: a low log cottage and a little cowshed. A narrow path zigzags down past the Neighbour's farm to a small market town by a frozen river, along a snowy road lined with birches and sheaves of oats on poles. Gudbrand and his wife have three small children: a boy of about eight with short black hair and a green jumper, a girl of about six with two stubby fair plaits and a red dress, and a chubby toddler in a long white shirt. The animals: a black cow with a white face, a sandy-yellow fjord horse with a striped pale mane, a fat pink pig, a white nanny goat, a woolly white sheep, a big white goose and a cinnamon-brown rooster.

This story's season, light and colours: The week before Christmas in clear, frosty weather: deep snow on the steep hillside, the fields and the turf roofs, short days of pale lemon-yellow sunshine with long blue shadows, and a pink glow when the sun goes down. Then a clear, deep-indigo night full of stars, with every small window glowing candle-yellow. Inside the cottage: warm firelight, straw ornaments and red-and-white cloths. Accents: the Wife's cornflower-blue apron and bright red rowan berries.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Gutten og fanden gutfand · 2/2 pictures

Knekk, knekk, knekk! En gutt går bortover veien og knekker nøtter.

Alt: En gutt i rød vest går bortover en høstvei og knekker nøtter. Bak en hasselbusk kommer en liten, rød skikkelse med horn og hale listende og smiler lurt.

On a country road in golden autumn evening light, the Boy strolls along cracking a walnut in his hands, his pockets bulging with more and a trail of cracked shells behind him. Beside the road the Little Devil comes tiptoeing out from behind a hazel bush with his chest puffed out and a sly, smug grin, his tufted tail curling up behind him. Russet leaves drift down, and far along the road a small smithy puffs smoke from its chimney.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):

- the Little Devil: A small, skinny imp no taller than a toddler, with dusty, matte brick-red skin, a narrow, pointy face with a sharp, beardless chin, narrow, sly green eyes under thin arched eyebrows, a wide, smug grin, big pointed ears and two tiny stubby horns like little thorns. Silly, not scary.

The boy eats walnuts: big, round, wrinkly, light-brown walnuts. The special nut is one of them, with one tiny round hole in its shell, which the boy plugs with a little wooden peg. By the road stands the smithy: a small, low log smithy with a turf roof and a stone chimney, a wide open door, a glowing forge with leather bellows, a big black anvil on a tree stump and a rack of hammers from tiny to huge, the biggest a sledgehammer as long as a man's leg.

This story's season, light and colours: An autumn evening: low amber sunlight and long shadows on the road, golden and russet hazel leaves, and a violet-blue dusk sky with the first star. Inside and around the smithy: the orange glow of the forge fire and a hanging lantern against sooty dark walls, with sparks and swirling dust.

#02 · gutten, fanden, smeden
child-friendly · after paragraph 17
Nøtta sprakk i tusen biter, og taket hoppet opp og landet igjen, litt på skjeve. Ut av skallbitene tumlet Fanden, med halen først. Han så seg forvirret rundt og pilte ut døra så støvet sto. Siden har ingen sett ham på den veien.

KNAS! PANG! Ut tumler Fanden, og han piler av sted så støvet står.

Alt: Taket på smia har hoppet opp og landet på skjeve. Fanden piler ut døra og bortover veien i en sky av støv, mens smeden måper med slegga i døråpningen og gutten smiler.

Outside the little log smithy at dusk: its turf roof has just jumped up and landed crooked, and dust puffs out from under the eaves. Out of the open door, lit orange by the forge fire, the Little Devil, back to his normal small size, scampers away down the road in a cloud of dust, looking back over his shoulder with a baffled face, his tufted tail flying. In the doorway the Smith stands gaping with the big sledgehammer in his hands, and beside him the Boy grins with his hands in his pockets. Bits of walnut shell lie on the doorstep.

Om gutten som gikk til nordavinden og krevde melet tilbake guttnord · 8/8 pictures

On a windswept, snowy mountain ridge under a cold blue-grey sky, the Boy stands with his feet planted wide and his fists on his hips, looking up at the enormous face of the North Wind, which fills the sky above him, cheeks puffed out and eyebrows bristling, blowing a gust of snowflakes at him. Picture: On a windswept, snowy mountain ridge under a cold blue-grey sky, the Boy stands with his feet planted wide and his fists on his hips, looking up at the enormous face of the North Wind, which fills the sky above him, cheeks puffed out and eyebrows bristling, blowing a gust of snowflakes at him. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Boy: A small, skinny boy of about nine with a narrow, pale face, cheeks rosy from the cold, big sticking-out ears, bright blue eyes, a determined little frown and white-blond hair that sticks up in tufts. He wears a baggy grey knitted jumper that is too big for him, patched dark-brown trousers, thick grey wool stockings, worn leather boots and a long brown knitted scarf.
- the North Wind: A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey clouds, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, big bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache made of snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft cloud hands. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his hair.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in the first cold weeks of winter. The boy and his mother live in a small, grey, weathered log cottage with a turf roof; beside it stands a little stabbur, a storehouse on posts with a steep wooden stair up to its door. Far away, on top of a high, snowy mountain with a few wind-bent spruces, lives the North Wind. By the road home lies the inn, a big, low log house with a lantern at the door and a goat shed behind. The magic cloth is a square white linen tablecloth with a red woven zigzag border, and the swapped one looks exactly the same. The stick is a knobbly old stick of pale birch wood, about as long as the boy is tall. The flour is carried in a small grey sack.

This story's season, light and colours: The first cold weeks of winter: a thin, new layer of snow on frozen ground, hoarfrost on every twig, blustery wind and cold blue-grey skies with fast grey clouds; deep snow on the North Wind's mountain. Indoors: warm, golden firelight and candlelight against the cold blue light at the windows.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Characters

Gutten gutten · the Boy

En hjelpsom og modig gutt som vil gjøre det rette for å skaffe mat til moren sin.

A small, skinny boy of about nine with a narrow, pale face, cheeks rosy from the cold, big sticking-out ears, bright blue eyes, a determined little frown and white-blond hair that sticks up in tufts. He wears a baggy grey knitted jumper that is too big for him, patched dark-brown trousers, thick grey wool stockings, worn leather boots and a long brown knitted scarf.

Moren moren · the Mother

En gammel, sliten mor som gutten passer på, og som blir lettet når de endelig får hjelp.

A thin, tired old woman of about sixty-five, a little stooped, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured wool dress, a darned brown knitted cardigan, a long patched linen apron and wooden clogs.

Nordavinden nordavinden · the North Wind

En kraftig, men rettferdig vind som kan virke brummete, men som gir gutten magiske gaver når han ber om hjelp.

A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey clouds, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, big bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache made of snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft cloud hands. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his hair.

Gjestgiveren gjestgiveren · the Innkeeper

En lur vert som prøver å bytte til seg de magiske tingene, men lærer å gjøre opp for seg.

A tall, gangly innkeeper of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small glittering eyes, a long pointed chin and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red waistcoat with shiny brass buttons over a white shirt with rolled sleeves, a long blue-and-white striped apron, dark breeches and a wide black leather money belt that jingles with coins.

Den magiske bukken bukken · the Billy Goat

En liten bukk som kan lage gull når gutten sier de rette ordene.

A small, sturdy billy goat about as big as a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail, neat black hooves and a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells.

The Cow rolls her eyes up towards them with a patient look. Fresh early-morning light, with the cowshed and the birch wood behind.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Cow: A gentle, sturdy old Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe running all along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long dark eyelashes, and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. A small brass bell hangs on a leather strap around her neck. She chews her cud slowly and never hurries.
- the Rooster: A sleek, swaggering rooster with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green in the sun, a tall, jagged scarlet comb standing straight up, long dangling wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs with long toes, and a fountain of long, curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He struts about with his head held high and loves the sound of his own voice.
- the Cuckoo: A slim, sleek cuckoo, smaller than a rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round, sleepy, half-closed eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base, and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up on the back of his head.
- the Black Grouse: A large, calm black grouse cock, a little bigger than a rooster, with glossy blue-black plumage, a bright-red fleshy arch like an eyebrow above each eye, a white bar across each wing, a fluffy snow-white puff of feathers under his tail, and a lyre-shaped tail whose two outer feathers curl outwards like hooks. He has feathered grey legs, a short black beak and wise, kind dark eyes, and stands tall and dignified like a judge.

Setting:
- the Little Farm: A small farm at the edge of a birch wood: a low grey log cowshed with a grass roof and a wide doorway, a little wooden ladder leading up to a hen hatch in its wall, a big, soft heap of golden straw against its side, a tall, weathered wooden gatepost with a flat top beside the straw, a grey split-rail fence, a dewy green meadow sloping down to white-stemmed birches, and a purple-brown heather moor rising on the hill beyond.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, where farm animals and wild birds can talk. On a small farm at the edge of a birch wood, the rooster, the cuckoo and the black grouse have bought one cow together. The rooster's home is a little hen hatch with a ladder in the cowshed wall, the cuckoo's home is a tall birch tree in the wood, and the black grouse's home is the purple-brown heather moor on the hill above. At night the three birds sleep on the big heap of golden straw beside the cowshed, next to the cow. The birds and the cow are natural animals without clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: Sunrise on an early-summer morning: a blazing saffron-and-gold sky with the sun coming up over the heather moor, long cool-blue shadows, thin silver mist lying in the hollows, and every feather rimmed with golden light. The opening picture is set in soft, warm afternoon light instead.

Characters

Hanen hanen · the Rooster

En ivrig og stolt hane som våkner først og blir veldig glad for å ha vunnet leken.

A sleek, swaggering rooster with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green in the sun, a tall, jagged scarlet comb standing straight up, long dangling wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs with long toes, and a fountain of long, curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He struts about with his head held high and loves the sound of his own voice.

Gjøken gjoken · the Cuckoo

En litt søvnig, men bestemt gjøk som våkner av hanens rop og vil gjerne ha sin del.

A slim, sleek cuckoo, smaller than a rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round, sleepy, half-closed eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base, and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up on the back of his head.

Århanen arhanen · the Black Grouse

En stor og rolig århane som foreslår en rettferdig løsning når de andre blir uenige.

A large, calm black grouse cock, a little bigger than a rooster, with glossy blue-black plumage, a bright-red fleshy arch like an eyebrow above each eye, a white bar across each wing, a fluffy snow-white puff of feathers under his tail, and a lyre-shaped tail whose two outer feathers curl outwards like hooks. He has feathered grey legs, a short black beak and wise, kind dark eyes, and stands tall and dignified like a judge.

Kua kua · the Cow

Den rolige kua som alle tre fuglene har kjøpt sammen, og som blir midtpunktet for leken og delingen.

A gentle, sturdy old Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe running all along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long dark eyelashes, and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. A small brass bell hangs on a leather strap around her neck. She chews her cud slowly and never hurries.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Hen: A plump, round, busy farm hen with soft chestnut-brown feathers, a darker brown neck laced with fine golden edges, a tiny wavy red comb, round amber eyes, a short pale-yellow beak and a short, upturned tail. - the Rooster: A tall, handsome farm rooster speckled all over in rust-red and bright gold like autumn leaves, with a shining golden cape of neck feathers, a fluffy golden beard puffing out under his beak, a small red comb, kind hazel eyes, a yellow beak, sturdy yellow legs and a sweeping tail of long, dark bronze feathers. - the Farmyard: A small, muddy farmyard on a hillside: a little red-painted henhouse on short stilts with a wooden ramp and a tiny door, a stacked woodpile with a chopping block, a grey split-rail fence with an open gate, shining puddles and a few patches of melting snow. Through the gate, a muddy road winds down past bare birches towards a small town far away in the valley, with a white church and red and yellow houses.

The hen's egg basket is a small, round wicker basket with a handle, lined with straw and holding exactly six light-brown eggs. The hen and the rooster are natural birds without clothes, and the hen is barefoot; she carries her basket hooked over one wing.

Characters

Hønen honen · the Hen

En flittig høne som verper egg hver dag, går barbeint og har ventet på skoene sine i år etter år.

A plump, round, busy farm hen with soft chestnut-brown feathers, a darker brown neck laced with fine golden edges, a tiny wavy red comb, round amber eyes, a short pale-yellow beak and a short, upturned tail. Her bare, bright-yellow feet are big, with long, spread-out toes. She carries a small round wicker basket lined with straw over one wing.

Hanen hanen · the Rooster

En omsorgsfull hane som vil hjelpe, og som foreslår en enkel og positiv plan så Hønen kan få det bedre.

A tall, handsome farm rooster speckled all over in rust-red and bright gold like autumn leaves, with a shining golden cape of neck feathers, a fluffy golden beard puffing out under his beak, a small red comb, kind hazel eyes, a yellow beak, sturdy yellow legs and a sweeping tail of long, dark bronze feathers. He looks gentle and a little sheepish, and likes to point with one wing.

Herreper herreper · 11/11 pictures

Katten rir ut av skogen og styrer reinsdyret med hornene.

Alt: En grå katt sitter mellom hornene på et stort reinsdyr og styrer med dem som med et sykkelstyre. Ved siden av går Per og måper.

The Cat sits proudly between the wide antlers of a big grey-brown reindeer, holding them like the handlebars of a bicycle, as the reindeer trots out of a sunny spruce forest towards the viewer. - the Cat: A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little bigger than an ordinary house cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest and chin, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and a long striped tail that she holds high. - Per: A lanky, kind-hearted boy of about seventeen with a long neck, gangly arms, a gentle oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair pulled back in a short ponytail. Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. Per's parents' tiny grey cottage stands empty at the edge of a spruce forest. The king's farm is a cluster of red-painted log buildings with turf roofs, a great log hall and a busy kitchen full of copper pots. A long country road winds from there over green hills, past pastures with sheep, cows and horses, to the Glittering Castle, where everything inside is gold. The pot is a round black iron pot, the griddle a big, flat, round iron griddle with a handle, and the cat's little gift box is tied with a red bow. The shining carriage is a small golden coach drawn by four white horses. The golden scissors are small and fine.

Characters

Per per · Per

Den yngste broren som starter med nesten ingenting, men vinner frem med godhet, mot og vilje til å gjøre det rette.

A lanky, kind-hearted boy of about seventeen with a long neck, gangly arms, a gentle oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile and chestnut hair pulled back in a short ponytail. He wears a grey wool coat far too big for him, with the sleeves rolled up several times and patched elbows, over a faded blue shirt, baggy brown trousers and worn-out shoes tied with string, and a shapeless oatmeal knitted cap.

Herreper herreper · Sir Per

Per i fine klær, med grønn jakke med gullknapper, rød kappe og hatt med fjær. Han sier alltid at han har det finere hjemme, for det har katten sagt at han skal si.

Per dressed up as the fine lord Herreper: the same lanky boy of about seventeen with a gentle oval face, soft brown eyes, a shy smile and chestnut hair in a short ponytail, now standing a little taller. He wears a bright green jacket with shiny gold buttons, a flowing scarlet cape fastened with a gold clasp, a broad hat with a long curling white feather, cream breeches and tall brown boots.

Katten (den forheksede prinsessen) katten · the Cat

En klok og hjelpsom katt som planlegger gavene, leder Per trygt frem, og viser seg å være en prinsesse som trenger å bli fri fra en trylleformel.

A clever, dignified grey tabby cat, a little bigger than an ordinary house cat, with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest and chin, big green-gold eyes, long white whiskers and a long striped tail that she holds high. Around her neck she wears an old, worn collar of faded red leather with a small tarnished brass buckle. She sits very upright, like a little queen.

Katten i hatt og kappe katten-pyntet · the Dressed-up Cat

Katten i sin egen lille hatt og kappe. Hun løper foran vogna, deler ut sølvskjeer og vet alltid hva som skal skje.

The same clever grey tabby cat with dark silver-grey stripes, four snow-white paws, a white chest, big green-gold eyes and her old faded red leather collar, now dressed up like Per: a tiny scarlet cape fastened at her throat and a little green hat with a curling white feather perched jauntily between her ears. She sits upright and proud, with her striped tail held high.

Prinsessen prinsessen · the Princess

Prinsessen som vokteren tryllet om til katt. Når Per klipper av halsbåndet, blir hun seg selv igjen, med langt, gyllent hår, og hun synger mye finere enn før.

A graceful young princess of about eighteen with a small pointed chin, high cheekbones, almond-shaped green-gold eyes like a cat's, a little upturned nose and very long, straight golden hair falling to her knees, with one silver-grey streak at her left temple. She wears a dove-grey silk gown with snow-white cuffs and a white lace collar, soft silver embroidery at the hem, and a thin silver circlet.

Kongen kongen · the King

En nysgjerrig og gavmild konge som blir imponert av gavene fra den mystiske Herreper og ønsker å se rikdommen med egne øyne.

A short, very fat king of about sixty with a round, shiny bald head, a tiny gold crown perched right on top, bulging cheeks, a red nose, small beady eyes and a huge drooping grey walrus moustache that hides his mouth. He wears a purple velvet robe with a spotted ermine collar stretched tight over his enormous belly, a wide gold belt, white stockings and pointed red shoes, and he usually looks grumpy.

Den forheksede vokteren vokteren · the Troll Guardian

Et stort, loddent troll som vokter slottet om natta og blir til stein når katten lurer ham til å se sola.

An enormous, round, woolly troll about four times as tall as a man, covered from head to toe in long, tangled, oatmeal-beige fur like a giant unshorn sheep. Two round yellow eyes glow like lanterns above a huge pink potato nose and a wide, soft mouth with two blunt buck teeth. He has tiny round ears, a long cow's tail with a tuft at the end and huge, flat, hairy bare feet. Silly and lonely rather than scary.

Tall arched windows look out towards the three gates, a wide golden fireplace stands at one end, and the floor is polished golden wood.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. Per's parents' tiny grey cottage stands empty at the edge of a spruce forest. The king's farm is a cluster of red-painted log buildings with turf roofs, a great log hall and a busy kitchen full of copper pots. A long country road winds from there over green hills, past pastures with sheep, cows and horses, to the Glittering Castle, where everything inside is gold. The pot is a round black iron pot, the griddle a big, flat, round iron griddle with a handle, and the cat's little gift box is tied with a red bow. The shining carriage is a small golden coach drawn by four white horses. The golden scissors are small and fine.

This story's season, light and colours: Bright high summer: deep-blue skies with fat white clouds, lush green hills and meadows full of buttercups, and dazzling sunshine that makes every silver and gold thing sparkle. The one night at the castle is deep violet-blue with warm golden candlelight, and the dawn that ends it glows peach and rose over the ridge. Accent colours: dove-grey, scarlet and glittering gold.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Jenta vokser opp hos fostermoren i et lyst og stille hus.

Alt: Fostermoren i dypblått slør og den lille jenta med lys flette går hånd i hånd mot et hvitt hus med røde blomster i vinduene.

The Foster Mother and the Little Girl walk hand in hand up a flower-lined path towards a bright, whitewashed house with red geraniums in every window. The Little Girl skips along and looks up at her with a big, happy smile, and the Foster Mother smiles down at her. Behind the house rises the great dark-green forest, and soft rose-and-gold evening light falls over everything.

The foster mother's house is a bright, quiet, whitewashed house with pale wooden floors and red geraniums in every window. In its hallway are three small, child-height doors of pale wood side by side, each with a little carved heart. Behind them wait a glittering silver-white star the size of an apple, a big, round, silver-white moon and a small, blazing golden sun. Far across the forest, a clear spring lies below a tall old oak, close to a storybook castle of pale sandstone with steep slate-blue roofs and round towers. The babies are wrapped in white shawls and sleep in a carved wooden cradle.

This story's season, light and colours: Mild, still spring: fresh pale-green birch leaves, white cherry blossom and lilac; pearly-pink dawns with mist over the spring, rose-and-lavender dusks, and deep-indigo nights with soft silver light. The foster mother's house glows creamy white and pale gold. Accents: the silver of the star and the moon, the warm gold of the sun and the deep blue of the foster mother's veil.

Characters

Fostermoren (Jomfru Maria) fostermoren · the Foster Mother

En mild og rettferdig fostermor som setter grenser, lærer jenta å holde det hun lover, og til slutt gir tilbake det som ble tatt og gjør alt godt igjen.

A tall, slender, serene woman of about thirty-five with an oval face, calm dark-brown eyes, a straight nose, softly arched dark brows and a gentle, quiet smile. Her dark hair is hidden under a long deep-blue veil that falls to her shoulders. She wears a long, simple cream-white gown with a band of silver embroidery at the hem, a deep-blue mantle fastened at the throat with a small silver lily brooch, and soft grey shoes.

Jenta som liten jenta-liten · the Little Girl

Den lille jenta som vokser opp hos fostermoren i det lyse huset, og som ikke klarer å la være å kikke bak de små dørene.

A small, slender girl of about eight with a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, big curious grey-green eyes, rosy cheeks and long ash-blonde hair in a single loose plait tied with a coral-pink ribbon. She wears a simple peach-coloured linen dress with short puffed sleeves and a white pinafore apron, and she goes barefoot.

Jenta jenta · the Girl

Jenta når hun er blitt stor: så vakker at det nesten lyser av henne, men hun kan ikke si et eneste ord.

A tall, slender, lovely girl of about seventeen with a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large grey-green eyes with dark lashes and a soft, gentle smile. Her long ash-blonde hair falls loose to her waist, held back by a thin coral-pink ribbon. She wears a simple peach-coloured linen dress with a laced rose-brown bodice and soft brown leather shoes.

Jenta (den unge dronningen) den-unge-dronningen · the Young Queen

En snill og nysgjerrig jente som vokser opp hos en mild fostermor, mister stemmen en tid, men finner mot, kjærlighet og glede igjen.

A lovely young queen of about nineteen with a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large grey-green eyes with dark lashes and a gentle smile, and long ash-blonde hair falling loose down her back under a slim silver crown set with small pearls. She wears a long, flowing apricot silk gown with wide sleeves, silver embroidery at the neckline and a white lace collar, and soft silver slippers.

Prinsen prinsen · the Prince

En godhjertet prins som stoler på den unge dronningen og står ved hennes side når andre tviler.

A tall, friendly young prince of about twenty-three with a long, open face, a strong straight nose, warm hazel eyes that crinkle when he smiles, wavy light-brown hair swept back to the nape of his neck and a short, neatly trimmed light-brown beard. He wears a knee-length teal-blue coat with silver buttons over a pale-grey shirt, charcoal breeches, soft black boots and a thin silver circlet on his head.

Den gamle dronningen den-gamle-dronningen · the Old Queen

Prinsens mor som først er streng og mistenksom, men lærer å skamme seg, forstå og vise kjærlighet når sannheten kommer fram.

A short, stout, stiff-backed old queen of about sixty-five with a round double chin, a haughty little upturned nose, small sharp black eyes, thin pencilled eyebrows and pursed lips. Her silver-white hair is piled high in stiff curls under a heavy gold crown set with red stones. She wears a high-necked deep-purple velvet gown with a stiff white ruff collar, and holds a gold lorgnette on a stick for peering at people.
