The ox strides forward, calm and strong, and she gazes out over the forests in wonder.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Princess: A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. She wears a faded, much-mended dress of pale sage-green wool with thin gold trim at the neck and cuffs, a grey knitted shawl and worn brown leather shoes, and carries a small birch-bark basket on her arm.
- the Blue Ox: A huge, gentle ox, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, deep cornflower-blue coat that shines like polished enamel, a paler blue muzzle, big soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving upwards with rounded tips, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel, and dark grey hooves. Calm, kind and very strong.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The princess grows up at her father's long, white-painted timber palace, with a red cowshed and forest pastures around it. The blue ox keeps a small white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it fills itself with food. Far away lie three magic forests: one of copper, where every trunk and leaf is polished copper and clinks in the wind; one of silver, whose leaves tinkle like little bells; and one of gold, where gold drips from the leaves like honey. Each troll carries a curved cow horn of healing salve on a string at its belt. Beyond the forests, a steep rock wall looks down on the prince's huge castle of pale-grey stone with green copper roofs, with a small pigsty below it and a dark stave church nearby. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Cool, clear early autumn under high, pale-blue skies: blue-grey fells, silver birches just turning yellow and purple heather, with the ox's deep, glossy blue as the strongest colour until the magic forests blaze in polished copper, frosty silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen is dim, warm and sooty; the church Sundays are fresh and green.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Kongsdattera som må gjete kyrne på tørre brødskalker, og som får en god venn i den blå oksen. Senere kaller hun seg Kari Trestakk.

A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. She wears a faded, much-mended dress of pale sage-green wool with thin gold trim at the neck and cuffs, a grey knitted shawl and worn brown leather shoes, and carries a small birch-bark basket on her arm.

Kari Trestakk kari-trestakk · Kari Trestakk

Ei snill prinsesse som rømmer fra den nye dronninga på ryggen av den blå oksen, og som vasker opp på et fremmed slott i en klaprende kjole av tre.

A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows and a dimple in her chin, her face and hands smudged with black soot and her long, wavy copper hair in a messy braid dulled with ash. Over a plain grey shift she wears the trestakk: a stiff, bell-shaped dress of rough, narrow grey-brown wooden slats laced together with rope, reaching from her shoulders to her ankles, and wooden clogs.

Kari i kobberkjolen kari-kobberkjole · Kari in the Copper Gown

Kari den første søndagen, i en kjole som skinner som kobberskogen, på vei til kirka på en hvit hest.

A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair falling loose down her back under a thin copper band. She wears a long, flowing gown of shining copper cloth that glows warm orange-pink like polished copper, embroidered with small copper leaves, with long copper-coloured gloves and soft copper slippers.

Kari i sølvkjolen kari-solvkjole · Kari in the Silver Gown

Kari den andre søndagen, i en kjole som glitrer som sølvskogen, på en hest med sølv på salen.

A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair in one loose braid woven with silver ribbons. She wears a long gown of shimmering silver cloth that glitters like frost, trimmed with rows of tiny silver leaves like little bells, a short silver-grey riding cape and silver slippers.

Kari i gullkjolen kari-gullkjole · Kari in the Gold Gown

Kari den tredje søndagen, i den fineste kjolen av alle, av gull og glitrende steiner, med små sko av gull.

A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair flowing loose under a thin gold circlet. She wears a long, full gown of gold cloth sewn all over with small glittering clear stones that sparkle like dew, and two small, pointed shoes of shining gold.

Den blå oksen blaa-oksen · the Blue Ox

En stor, blank okse med en matduk i øret, som bærer prinsessa gjennom skogene av kobber, sølv og gull og stanger trollene av veien.

A huge, gentle ox, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, deep cornflower-blue coat that shines like polished enamel, a paler blue muzzle, big soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving upwards with rounded tips, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel, and dark grey hooves. Calm, kind and very strong.

Prinsen prinsen · the Prince

En prins som jager kjøkkenjenta i trestakken ut av døra tre søndager på rad, men ikke klarer å ta øynene fra den fine jenta i kirka.

A broad-shouldered prince of about twenty with a proud, stubborn face, a strong jaw, a slightly hooked nose, bright blue eyes under straight fair brows, and thick, wavy honey-blond hair swept back from his forehead and falling to his collar, under a small gold crown. He wears a heather-purple velvet doublet with gold buttons, a cream linen shirt with a ruffled collar, a short dark-green cape fastened with a round gold brooch, black breeches and soft black leather boots.

Den nye dronninga den-nye-dronninga · the New Queen

Kongens nye kone, som setter prinsessa til å gjete kyrne på tørre brødskalker og later som hun er syk for å få spise den blå oksen.

A tall, thin queen of about forty with a long, pinched face, a sharp pointed nose, narrow pale-green eyes, thin arched eyebrows, a small mouth turned down at the corners and jet-black hair scraped into a tight bun under a tall, spiky silver crown. She wears a stiff, high-collared gown of dark slate-grey silk with a white lace ruff, a black velvet cape and many rings, and holds a lace handkerchief.

Dattera til dronninga dattera-til-dronninga · the Queen's Daughter

Den nye dronningas datter, så sur at melka surner bare hun går forbi fjøset. Hun vil så gjerne få gullskoen på.

A gangly girl of about sixteen with a long, sour face, a pinched, turned-up nose, small squinting pale-green eyes, a pouting mouth and thin, straw-pale hair in two stiff braids that stick out sideways. She wears a frilly dress the sour green of unripe gooseberries, covered in too many pink bows, white stockings, and pointed green shoes on very long, big feet.

Mannen i berget mannen-i-berget · the Old Man of the Mountain

En gammel mann med langt, hvitt skjegg og grønn kappe, som kommer ut når Kari banker på berget, og gir henne kjoler av kobber, sølv og gull og en hest til kirka.

A small, sturdy old man, no taller than a girl of fifteen, with a round, rosy, wrinkled face, a big round nose, twinkling bright-blue eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a long, silky white beard that reaches his knees. He wears a long, hooded moss-green cloak with a wooden toggle, a brown tunic with a rope belt and soft brown boots, and carries a small brass lantern that glows warm yellow.

Trollet med tre hoder trollet-med-tre-hoder · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet i kobberskogen. Alle tre hodene brøler når noen rører skogen, men til slutt sitter det til halsen i myra.

A squat, pot-bellied troll about twice as tall as a man, with chalk-white, lumpy skin speckled with grey freckles and patches of moss, short bandy legs and long dangling arms. It has three bald, egg-shaped heads on three thick necks, each with a big red bulbous nose, small round orange eyes, one crooked tooth and tufts of stiff orange hair behind the ears. It wears a ragged brown sacking kilt, with a curved cow horn of salve hanging from its rope belt.

Trollet med seks hoder trollet-med-seks-hoder · the Six-Headed Troll

Trollet i sølvskogen, dobbelt så sterkt som det første. De seks hodene kjefter på hverandre når det henger fast i et sølvtre.

A tall, lanky troll about three times as tall as a man, with bright pumpkin-orange, knobbly skin patched with grey lichen, long skinny arms and legs and huge flat feet. On a wide, bony pair of shoulders sit six small heads, each with a long droopy nose, sleepy yellow eyes, big flappy ears and wispy white hair like dandelion fluff. It wears a moth-eaten grey wool tunic, with a curved cow horn of salve hanging on a string from its belt.

Trollet med ni hoder trollet-med-ni-hoder · the Nine-Headed Troll

Trollet i gullskogen, så stort at det skygger for sola. Det blåser seg opp og seiler av sted som en diger, sint ballong.

An enormous, pear-shaped troll as tall as six men, with rosy heather-pink, lumpy skin, a huge round belly and short, stumpy arms and legs. Along its broad shoulders sit nine small round heads in a row, each with puffy cheeks, a tiny snub nose, small black eyes under bushy grey eyebrows, big round ears and a shock of spiky grey hair. It wears a huge patched brown hide tunic, with a curved cow horn of salve hanging from its belt.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Princess: A slender girl of about fifteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The princess grows up at her father's long, white-painted timber palace, with a red cowshed and forest pastures around it. The blue ox keeps a small white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it fills itself with food. Far away lie three magic forests: one of copper, where every trunk and leaf is polished copper and clinks in the wind; one of silver, whose leaves tinkle like little bells; and one of gold, where gold drips from the leaves like honey. The castle kitchen is dim, warm and sooty; the church Sundays are fresh and green.

The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Far away lie three magic forests: one of copper, where every trunk and leaf is polished copper and clinks in the wind; one of silver, whose leaves tinkle like little bells; and one of gold, where gold drips from the leaves like honey. Each troll carries a curved cow horn of healing salve on a string at its belt. Beyond the forests, a steep rock wall looks down on the prince's huge castle of pale-grey stone with green copper roofs, with a small pigsty below it and a dark stave church nearby. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Cool, clear early autumn under high, pale-blue skies: blue-grey fells, silver birches just turning yellow and purple heather, with the ox's deep, glossy blue as the strongest colour until the magic forests blaze in polished copper, frosty silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen is dim, warm and sooty; the church Sundays are fresh and green.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Lillekort: A tiny, bold little boy, no bigger than a four-year-old child, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined chin and a mop of golden curls. On his head sits an oversized knitted cap with blue-and-white stripes, flopping over one ear. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a huge, faded blue linen smock covered in patches, hanging to his knees like a nightshirt and tied at the waist with a piece of rope, and enormous, floppy old leather boots.
- the Five-Headed Troll: A huge, hunched sea troll five times as tall as a man, with dusky purple-grey skin like a mussel shell and a round hump of a back like an upturned boat, crusted with barnacles and seaweed. Exactly five heads poke out in a row from under the front of the hump, like turtles peeping out of a shell, each with a long drooping nose, small round yellow eyes and shaggy grey hair. It has long, dangling arms, flat flipper feet and an old fishing net knotted round its middle.
- Sir Red: A big, burly, barrel-chested knight of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair and a huge, bushy fiery-red beard. He wears polished steel armour that clanks with every step over a red tunic, a long bright-red cloak and heavy steel-capped boots, and always has a big white handkerchief tucked into his belt.

Setting:
- the Shore: A wide, pale sandy beach below the royal farm, curving along the open sea. Right at the water's edge lies one big, flat, grey boulder, and at the top of the beach stands a huge, gnarled old oak with wide, spreading branches and yellow-brown autumn leaves. Tufts of beach grass grow in the low dunes, and a grassy slope rises behind to the dark log buildings of the royal farm.

Story world: Old Norway, long ago, in late autumn. Lillekort is born in a tiny, crooked cottage with a sagging turf roof at the edge of a forest of yellow birches and red rowans. Far away, the royal farm stands on a slope above a sandy shore by the open sea: dark log buildings with turf roofs around a long hall, all hung with black cloth at first. Lillekort's sword has a shining golden hilt and hangs in a plain brown leather sheath. His magic ship is a wooden sailing ship with two masts and white sails; when it is small, it is no bigger than a slipper and fits in his pocket. The sea trolls come in black ships with black sails, and their hair is grey. The princess's three secret suits for Lillekort are of gold, silver and brass. The iron chain is huge, heavy and five hundred metres long.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn on the open coast: crisp, blustery days with yellow birch leaves and scarlet rowan berries whirling over a dark-green sea with white-capped waves. On the three Thursday nights a huge, low, orange harvest moon hangs over the shore and silver sea mist drifts across the sand. The royal farm is draped in black until the wedding, when candlelight makes gold, silver and brass glitter. Under the sea: cool green-blue water and the red-orange glow of the troll's brewing fire.

Den travle kokkejenta på kongsgården, som Lillekort bærer ved og vann for, og som får gullbånd og sølvbånd i stedet for ved.

A tall, gangly kitchen maid of about eighteen with long arms, a long, cheerful face, a big crooked smile, a long nose with a dab of flour on the tip, lively hazel eyes and one thick sandy-blonde braid hanging down her back. Her sleeves are rolled up. She wears a long violet wool dress and a big white apron with soup stains, and keeps a large wooden ladle tucked into her apron strings.

Trollet med fem hoder trollet-med-fem-hoder · the Five-Headed Troll

Det første trollet som kommer opp av havet for å hente prinsessa. Det er så stort at det skygger for månen.

A huge, hunched sea troll five times as tall as a man, with dusky purple-grey skin like a mussel shell and a round hump of a back like an upturned boat, crusted with barnacles and seaweed. Exactly five heads poke out in a row from under the front of the hump, like turtles peeping out of a shell, each with a long drooping nose, small round yellow eyes and shaggy grey hair. It has long, dangling arms, flat flipper feet and an old fishing net knotted round its middle.

Trollet med ti hoder trollet-med-ti-hoder · the Ten-Headed Troll

Det andre trollet, som kommer den neste torsdagen. Det er dobbelt så stort som det første.

An enormous sea troll about ten times as tall as a man, with rough, slate-blue skin, knobbly and shiny like wet rock, a broad, square body, short thick legs and huge webbed feet. It has exactly ten round heads in two neat rows of five, one row stacked above the other like eggs in a box; each head has a flat nose, big goggling green eyes, a wide frog mouth and a scraggly grey beard. It wears a torn black sail wrapped around its middle.

Trollet med femten hoder trollet-med-femten-hoder · the Fifteen-Headed Troll

Det tredje og største trollet av alle, så stort at det stenger for hele himmelen.

The biggest troll of all, as big as a mountain, with dark peat-brown, lumpy skin like a bog, shaggy grey hair on its shoulders, a round belly and legs like old tree stumps. It has exactly fifteen heads stacked in a pyramid: five on its shoulders, then four, three, two and one on top; each head has a round red nose, small blinking amber eyes and a shock of grey hair. It wears a huge patched brown sailcloth tunic tied with a ship's rope.

Trollet på havets bunn sjotrollet · the Sea Troll

Trollet som bor i et fjell på havets bunn og har holdt den eldste prinsessa fanget. Det brøler før det tenker, men er lett å lure.

A fat, grumpy troll about three times as tall as a man, with smooth, shiny turquoise skin like a wet fish, a barrel belly, short bowed legs and big flat webbed feet. He has one huge head with a gigantic, wrinkly, trumpet-shaped nose that is always sniffing, bulging pale-orange eyes, bristly orange eyebrows and a long tangle of brown kelp for hair and beard. He wears baggy patched sailcloth breeches held up by a rope and a necklace of big shells.

Outside a tiny, crooked cottage with a sagging turf roof at the edge of an autumn forest, Lillekort strolls out of the door and down the path, chin up and happy as a lark, a little lunch bundle tied to a stick over his shoulder. In the doorway behind him his mother, a thin, tired woman in a grey dress and a brown headscarf, throws up her hands in astonishment, and seven older children crowd around her skirts, staring. Far down the road ahead, tiny Lavring is just trotting round a bend. Soft morning light.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Lillekort: A tiny, bold little boy, no bigger than a four-year-old child, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined chin and a mop of golden curls. On his head sits an oversized knitted cap with blue-and-white stripes, flopping over one ear. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a huge, faded blue linen smock covered in patches, hanging to his knees like a nightshirt and tied at the waist with a piece of rope, and enormous, floppy old leather boots.
- Lavring: A tiny, bold little boy, no bigger than a four-year-old child, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes and a mop of golden curls, exactly like his twin brother, and a cheeky, know-it-all grin. On his head sits an oversized knitted cap with red-and-white stripes. He wears his big brothers' old rags: a huge, patched mustard-yellow wool smock that hangs down to his knees, tied at the waist with a piece of rope, and big wooden clogs.

Story world: Old Norway, long ago, in late autumn. Lillekort is born in a tiny, crooked cottage with a sagging turf roof at the edge of a forest of yellow birches and red rowans. Far away, the royal farm stands on a slope above a sandy shore by the open sea: dark log buildings with turf roofs around a long hall, all hung with black cloth at first. Lillekort's sword has a shining golden hilt and hangs in a plain brown leather sheath. His magic ship is a wooden sailing ship with two masts and white sails; when it is small, it is no bigger than a slipper and fits in his pocket. The sea trolls come in black ships with black sails, and their hair is grey. The princess's three secret suits for Lillekort are of gold, silver and brass. The iron chain is huge, heavy and five hundred metres long.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn on the open coast: crisp, blustery days with yellow birch leaves and scarlet rowan berries whirling over a dark-green sea with white-capped waves. On the three Thursday nights a huge, low, orange harvest moon hangs over the shore and silver sea mist drifts across the sand. The royal farm is draped in black until the wedding, when candlelight makes gold, silver and brass glitter. Under the sea: cool green-blue water and the red-orange glow of the troll's brewing fire.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Sea Troll: A fat, grumpy troll about three times as tall as a man, with smooth, shiny turquoise skin like a wet fish, a barrel belly, short bowed legs and big flat webbed feet. He has one huge head with a gigantic, wrinkly, trumpet-shaped nose that is always sniffing, bulging pale-orange eyes, bristly orange eyebrows and a long tangle of brown kelp for hair and beard. He wears baggy patched sailcloth breeches held up by a rope and a necklace of big shells.
- the Eldest Princess: A tall, strong, broad-shouldered princess of about twenty, a head taller than her little sister and quick on her feet, with the same small, delicate face, pointed chin, tiny snub nose and big grey eyes, pink cheeks and thick platinum-blonde curls that tumble to her shoulders, held back with a string of pearls. - Lillekort in Gold: The same tiny, bold boy, no bigger than a four-year-old child, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes and a mop of golden curls under his oversized blue-and-white striped knitted cap. A tall, dark wooden cupboard stands against one wall, and a heavy round wooden door leads out into the green-blue sea.

Story world: Old Norway, long ago, in late autumn. Lillekort is born in a tiny, crooked cottage with a sagging turf roof at the edge of a forest of yellow birches and red rowans. Far away, a grassy mound with a round wooden door.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. At home: a small grey log farmhouse with a turf roof, a round stone well in the long grass in front, and a tiny pig-house of rough grey planks with one small window. Deep down the well lies another world: a wide green meadow with a low fence of woven hazel twigs, a big old apple tree with a kind face in its bark, and a path to the troll hag's farm, a grassy mound with a round wooden door. Her one room is dug into the earth: stone walls, roots hanging from the ceiling, a thick beam, and a plank table with a candle and a bowl of mushrooms. Her low, dark cowshed holds three black cows. The three chests are small wooden chests with curved lids: one red, one green, and one blue with three little white crosses on its lid.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. At home above the well: a grey, damp day under low clouds, with wet grass and muted greens, browns and greys. Down below the well: a dreamlike, sunlit world of everlasting summer, with jewel-bright green grass, a big, soft white-gold sun in a cloudless apricot-tinted sky, white clover and red apples. In the troll hag's earth house: dim, earthy browns lit by one candle. At the end, the pig-house glows with warm gold and pearly light. Accents: the Girl's blue headscarf and the red, green and blue chests.

Kone-datteren kone-datteren · the Stepsister

Den late og sta stesøsteren som vil ha belønning uten å vise omsorg, og som ofte velger lettvint i stedet for snilt.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered girl of about fourteen with a broad, square face, a heavy jaw, full lips pushed out in a sulk, a wide flat nose, small dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows drawn together in a scowl, and a big, bushy cloud of black frizzy hair tied on top with a red ribbon. She wears a fussy mustard-yellow dress with puffed sleeves and a ruffled white collar, shiny red shoes with buckles, and a small cloth pouch of raisins tied at her waist.

Stemoren stemoren · the Stepmother

Mannens nye kone og mor til Kone-datteren. Hun blir aldri fornøyd med Mannens datter og drømmer om vegger av gull.

A short, stout, bossy woman of about forty-five with a big, doughy face, heavy cheeks, a small snub nose, small cold black eyes, a sour little mouth and frizzy black hair streaked with grey, bundled into a big knot on top of her head. She wears a stiff dark-plum wool dress with a black bodice and a starched collar fastened with a large round silver brooch, and she usually stands with her arms folded.

Trollkjerringa trollkjerringa · the Troll Hag

En streng og smågretten gårdskone i den underjordiske gården som tester jentene med merkelige oppgaver, men lar dem dra med lønn til slutt.

A big, heavy, barrel-shaped troll woman, a head taller than a grown woman and twice as broad, with a wrinkled, sallow face, a very long, knobbly, hooked nose, one thick bushy grey eyebrow straight across her forehead, small squinting black eyes, a sour down-turned mouth and a wart on her chin. Stiff grey hair pokes out of a red headscarf tied under her chin. She wears a coarse charcoal-grey dress, a sacking apron and huge, clumpy clogs, and a tufted cow's tail peeks out under her skirt.

Småfuglene smafuglene · the Little Birds

Små, hjelpsomme fugler som synger vennlige råd og viser hvordan tålmodighet og omtanke kan løse vanskelige oppgaver.

A little flock of exactly three identical tiny songbirds, each no bigger than a plum: round and fluffy, with a sky-blue cap, wings and tail, a lemon-yellow breast, white cheeks with a thin black stripe through each eye, a short black beak, shiny black bead eyes and thin grey legs. They always stay together, sing with their beaks wide open and tilt their heads cheerfully.

Kua kua · the Cow

Den snille kua på den grønne enga, med ei bøtte på hornene. Hun vil bli melket, og siden gjemmer hun Mannens datter under magen sin.

A gentle, plump cow with a red-and-white spotted coat, long curved cream-coloured horns, big soft brown eyes with long lashes, a wet pink nose, a calm, friendly face, a swishing tail with a white tuft and pale hooves. A wooden milk bucket with a rope handle always hangs from one of her horns.

Bukken bukken · the Ram

En stor sauebukk med så mye ull at han ser ut som ei sky med bein. Han vil bli klipt, og siden gjemmer han Mannens datter under ullskjerfet sitt.

A big, round sheep ram so thick with creamy-white wool that he looks like a cloud on legs, with a black face, black legs, big curly golden-brown horns, sleepy half-closed amber eyes and a soft, silly smile. A big pair of iron sheep shears hangs from one of his horns.

A grey, damp day. In the long wet grass beside the round stone well in front of the small grey farmhouse, the Girl and the Stepsister sit spinning with wooden hand spindles. The Stepsister has a basket of soft, silky, pale-gold flax and a smug face; the Girl has a basket of stiff, prickly black pig bristles. A little white lamb has trotted over to sniff the Girl's basket, and she strokes its head with a smile. Behind them, the Stepmother stands with her arms folded, frowning at the lamb.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):

Her light-brown wavy hair curls to her shoulders from under a blue headscarf knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain, patched undyed linen dress, a faded brown pinafore and old brown shoes.
- the Stepsister: A sturdy, broad-shouldered girl of about fourteen with a broad, square face, a heavy jaw, full lips pushed out in a sulk, a wide flat nose, small dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows drawn together in a scowl, and a big, bushy cloud of black frizzy hair tied on top with a red ribbon. She wears a fussy mustard-yellow dress with puffed sleeves and a ruffled white collar, shiny red shoes with buckles, and a small cloth pouch of raisins tied at her waist.
- the Stepmother: A short, stout, bossy woman of about forty-five with a big, doughy face, heavy cheeks, a small snub nose, small cold black eyes, a sour little mouth and frizzy black hair streaked with grey, bundled into a big knot on top of her head. She wears a stiff dark-plum wool dress with a black bodice and a starched collar fastened with a large round silver brooch, and she usually stands with her arms folded.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. At home: a small grey log farmhouse with a turf roof, a round stone well in the long grass in front, and a tiny pig-house of rough grey planks with one small window. Deep down the well lies another world: a wide green meadow with a low fence of woven hazel twigs, a big old apple tree with a kind face in its bark, and a path to the troll hag's farm, a grassy mound with a round wooden door. Her one room is dug into the earth: stone walls, roots hanging from the ceiling, a thick beam, and a plank table with a candle and a bowl of mushrooms. Her low, dark cowshed holds three black cows. The three chests are small wooden chests with curved lids: one red, one green, and one blue with three little white crosses on its lid.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. At home above the well: a grey, damp day under low clouds, with wet grass and muted greens, browns and greys. Down below the well: a dreamlike, sunlit world of everlasting summer, with jewel-bright green grass, a big, soft white-gold sun in a cloudless apricot-tinted sky, white clover and red apples. In the troll hag's earth house: dim, earthy browns lit by one candle. At the end, the pig-house glows with warm gold and pearly light. Accents: the Girl's blue headscarf and the red, green and blue chests.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

Inside the troll hag's single room dug into the earth: stone walls, roots hanging from the low ceiling, a thick beam, and a plank table with one candle and a bowl of mushrooms. The Troll Hag stands behind the table with her arms folded, glaring down her long, knobbly nose. In the round doorway, with sunny green daylight behind her, the Girl stands politely with her hands clasped, looking up at her bravely. Funny rather than frightening.

Full prompt

- Image 1: model sheet for the Troll Hag, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Troll Hag's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Troll Hag only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 2: model sheet for the Girl, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Girl's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Girl only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Inside the troll hag's single room dug into the earth: stone walls, roots hanging from the low ceiling, a thick beam, and a plank table with one candle and a bowl of mushrooms. The Troll Hag stands behind the table with her arms folded, glaring down her long, knobbly nose. In the round doorway, with sunny green daylight behind her, the Girl stands politely with her hands clasped, looking up at her bravely. Funny rather than frightening.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Troll Hag: A big, heavy, barrel-shaped troll woman, a head taller than a grown woman and twice as broad, with a wrinkled, sallow face, a very long, knobbly, hooked nose, one thick bushy grey eyebrow straight across her forehead, small squinting black eyes, a sour down-turned mouth and a wart on her chin. Stiff grey hair pokes out of a red headscarf tied under her chin. She wears a coarse charcoal-grey dress, a sacking apron and huge, clumpy clogs, and a tufted cow's tail peeks out under her skirt.
- the Girl: A kind, patient girl of about thirteen, slim and a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle little face, big grey eyes, a tiny nose, pink cheeks and a shy smile. Her light-brown wavy hair curls to her shoulders from under a blue headscarf knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain, patched undyed linen dress, a faded brown pinafore and old brown shoes.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. At home: a small grey log farmhouse with a turf roof, a round stone well in the long grass in front, and a tiny pig-house of rough grey planks with one small window. Deep down the well lies another world: a wide green meadow with a low fence of woven hazel twigs, a big old apple tree with a kind face in its bark, and a path to the troll hag's farm, a grassy mound with a round wooden door. Her one room is dug into the earth: stone walls, roots hanging from the ceiling, a thick beam, and a plank table with a candle and a bowl of mushrooms. Her low, dark cowshed holds three black cows. The three chests are small wooden chests with curved lids: one red, one green, and one blue with three little white crosses on its lid.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. At home above the well: a grey, damp day under low clouds, with wet grass and muted greens, browns and greys. Down below the well: a dreamlike, sunlit world of everlasting summer, with jewel-bright green grass, a big, soft white-gold sun in a cloudless apricot-tinted sky, white clover and red apples. In the troll hag's earth house: dim, earthy browns lit by one candle. At the end, the pig-house glows with warm gold and pearly light. Accents: the Girl's blue headscarf and the red, green and blue chests.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:

- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Master Thief: A slim, nimble young man of about twenty with a narrow, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Setting:
- the Manor Farm: A large, prosperous farm around a big grassy yard with a stone well. On one side stands a grand two-storey manor house of white-painted timber with a dark hipped roof, rows of small-paned windows with green shutters, a carved front porch and a bed of red and yellow tulips under the upstairs windows. Around the yard stand a long red stable, a small red goose house and a kitchen wing, with blossoming apple trees and birches behind.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone at the edge of the woods. Deep in a dark spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dim timber house with a stone fireplace. The farmer walks his three oxen, big and gentle, reddish-brown with white faces and short curved horns, along the Forest Road. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm, with a goose house full of white geese and a long stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses with cream-and-black manes; he himself rides a big dapple-grey horse. The priest lives at the vicarage, with a huge old linden tree in the garden. The master thief's sack is a big patched brown sack, and the barrel is a big oak barrel on a small two-wheeled cart pulled by a bony old brown mare.

This story's season, light and colours: A blustery, rain-washed late spring: a stormy blue-black night at the start, then fresh leaf-green birches, apple blossom and tulips at the Manor Farm, and dusty, sunny country roads by day. Many of the tricks happen at dusk or at night, in deep indigo moonlight with warm amber lantern and candle glow, and the mornings come up rosy pink. Accent colours: the thief's bottle-green, brass and blossom pink.

Den yngste sønnen (Mestertyven) mestertyven · the Master Thief

Den yngste av tre brødre, en vennlig og oppfinnsom gutt som lærer å snike seg til ting, men som også har et godt hjerte og retter opp det som blir galt.

A slim, nimble young man of about twenty with a narrow, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey felt hat with a narrow brim, always worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, patched bottle-green coat with deep pockets over a cream shirt, a red neckerchief, narrow charcoal trousers and soft black boots.

Mestertyven i uniform mestertyven-general · the General

Mestertyven i en uniform med gullsnorer og blanke knapper, som han fant blant røverskattene. Slik rir han hjem til faren, som nesten ikke kjenner ham igjen.

The master thief dressed up as a grand general: the same slim young man of about twenty with a narrow, clever face, a sly lopsided grin, a thin black moustache and short curly black hair. He wears a black two-cornered hat with a white plume, a navy-blue uniform coat with two rows of shiny brass buttons, gold cords looped across the chest and gold-fringed epaulettes, a wide red sash, white breeches and tall polished black riding boots.

Mestertyven som fillegutt mestertyven-fillegutt · the Ragged Boy

Mestertyven forkledd som en fillete gutt med en sekk. Ingen ser noe rart ved ham, men i sekken har han tre levende harer.

The master thief disguised as a ragged beggar boy: the same slim young man with a narrow, clever face, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache, his cheeks smudged with dirt. He wears a torn, floppy straw hat, a baggy sackcloth smock full of holes and patches tied with string, and frayed trousers rolled up to the knees, and goes barefoot, with a big patched brown sack over one shoulder.

Mestertyven som engel mestertyven-engel · the Pretend Angel

Mestertyven med et hvitt laken over seg og vinger av gåsefjær på ryggen. Slik lurer han presten til å tro at han skal til himmelen.

The master thief disguised as an angel: the same slim young man with a narrow, clever face, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. A big white bed sheet is draped over his head and body like a long hooded robe, leaving his face free, and two huge home-made wings of grey-and-white goose feathers are tied onto his back with string, a little crooked. His bare feet peek out below the sheet.

Mestertyven som kjerring mestertyven-kjerring · the Beggar Crone

Mestertyven forkledd som ei gammel, krokete kjerring med stav og filler. Hun fryser så fælt og vil bare sitte litt innenfor stalldøra.

The master thief disguised as a crooked old beggar woman: a stooped, limping figure leaning on a knobbly wooden staff. A faded black headscarf is pulled low over a tangled grey wig, but a thin black moustache and a sly grin peek out underneath. She wears a patched grey horse blanket as a shawl, a ragged brown skirt that is too short, showing big muddy boots, and a torn apron with a deep pocket.

Mestertyven med geiteskjegg mestertyven-tonnemann · the Barrel Man

Mestertyven forkledd som en fillete mann med et stort, bustete skjegg av geitehår. Han skal i bryllup med ei tønne og holder fingeren i hullet hele tida.

The master thief disguised as a shabby old carter: the same slim young man with sly, narrow eyes, but his face is almost hidden behind a huge, bushy false beard of shaggy grey-white goat hair that reaches down to his belt. He wears a squashed, wide-brimmed black hat, a ragged mud-brown coat tied with rope, patched knee breeches and worn clogs.

Den gamle kona i huset gammel-kone · the Old Woman

En sliten, men godhjertet gammel kvinne som advarer gutten og håper han skal klare seg, og som til slutt blir møtt med takknemlighet.

A short, round, jolly old woman of about seventy with bright red apple cheeks, a button nose, twinkling blue eyes, deep laugh lines and wisps of white hair escaping from a red-and-white checked headscarf tied under her chin. She wears a long dark-brown wool dress with the sleeves pushed up, a wide sunflower-yellow apron with a big pocket and sturdy clogs, and keeps a big wooden ladle tucked into her apron strings.

Husmannen husmannen · the Cottager

Faren til mestertyven, en fattig husmann som ikke har noe å gi sønnene sine. Han er redd for fine folk, men sitter stolt øverst ved bordet i bryllupet.

A thin, timid old cottager of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare, patched mouse-brown smock tied with a cord, baggy patched trousers and old clogs, with a worn grey-and-blue striped blanket wrapped round his shoulders like a shawl.

Bonden med oksene bonden · the Farmer

En snill bonde som skal til byen og selge oksene sine, og som blir lurt tre ganger på den samme veien. Kona hans er så sur at han bare tør å plystre langt ute på jordet.

A big, broad, soft-hearted farmer of about forty with a round, sunburnt face, a bulbous red nose, small worried blue eyes, large ears and a short, curly light-brown beard. He wears a battered brown felt hat, a woolly sheepskin vest over a blue work shirt with rolled-up sleeves and brown trousers tucked into muddy boots, and carries a long coiled rope over one shoulder.

Amtmannen amtmannen · the Bailiff

En rik og selvsikker mann som setter prøver for å teste gutten, og som ender med å le av sin egen overraskelse og holde ord.

A stout, self-important gentleman of about fifty-five with a huge round belly, a pink double chin, rosy jowls, small twinkling eyes, a snub nose, a neat grey moustache waxed into two curly tips and grey hair curling over his ears. He wears a round-crowned black hat, a tobacco-brown frock coat with brass buttons over a canary-yellow waistcoat stretched tight across his belly, a gold watch chain, grey striped trousers and shiny black shoes.

Amtmannens datter amtmannens-datter · the Bailiff's Daughter

Amtmannens snille og kloke datter, som står i døra og smiler når faren setter den første prøven, og som til slutt selv sier ja til mestertyven.

A kind, clever young woman of about nineteen with a heart-shaped face, a dimple in one cheek, lively grey-green eyes that always seem to be laughing, a small straight nose and nut-brown hair in two braids coiled into round buns over her ears. She wears a long apricot-coloured dress with a white embroidered collar and puffed sleeves, and a sprig of white lily of the valley pinned at her collar.

Presten presten · the Priest

En stolt, men ufarlig skikkelse som blir lurt på en måte som mest er pinlig og morsom, og som lærer å være litt mer forsiktig.

A tall, stiff, very proud priest of about fifty with a long thin face, a long pointed nose held high, raised eyebrows, a small pursed mouth and a long, pointed sandy-grey beard. He wears a round, wide-brimmed black hat, a long black cassock buttoned to the chin, a big white pleated millstone ruff around his neck and black buckled shoes, and clasps a small black hymn book to his chest.

Picture: A wide view of a spot where a dirt road splits into three, one road winding into a dark spruce forest, one over a green hill and one along a river. The Cottager stands at the fork, wrapped in his striped blanket, waving goodbye with a wobbly smile. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Cottager: A thin, timid old cottager of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare, patched mouse-brown smock tied with a cord, baggy patched trousers and old clogs, with a worn grey-and-blue striped blanket wrapped round his shoulders like a shawl.
- the Master Thief: A slim, nimble young man of about twenty with a narrow, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone at the edge of the woods. Deep in a dark spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dim timber house with a stone fireplace. The farmer walks his three oxen, big and gentle, reddish-brown with white faces and short curved horns, along the Forest Road. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm, with a goose house full of white geese and a long stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses with cream-and-black manes; he himself rides a big dapple-grey horse. The priest lives at the vicarage, with a huge old linden tree in the garden. The master thief's sack is a big patched brown sack, and the barrel is a big oak barrel on a small two-wheeled cart pulled by a bony old brown mare.

This story's season, light and colours: A blustery, rain-washed late spring: a stormy blue-black night at the start, then fresh leaf-green birches, apple blossom and tulips at the Manor Farm, and dusty, sunny country roads by day. Many of the tricks happen at dusk or at night, in deep indigo moonlight with warm amber lantern and candle glow, and the mornings come up rosy pink. Accent colours: the thief's bottle-green, brass and blossom pink.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Setting:
- the Forest Road: A narrow, dusty dirt road winding through a light forest of white-trunked birches and dark spruces, with a grassy ditch along one side, big mossy grey stones and round green bushes at the roadside, and a weathered grey wooden rail fence where the road bends. Here and there a big old birch leans over the road with a thick, low branch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone at the edge of the woods. Deep in a dark spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dim timber house with a stone fireplace. The farmer walks his three oxen, big and gentle, reddish-brown with white faces and short curved horns, along the Forest Road. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm, with a goose house full of white geese and a long stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses with cream-and-black manes; he himself rides a big dapple-grey horse. The priest lives at the vicarage, with a huge old linden tree in the garden. The master thief's sack is a big patched brown sack, and the barrel is a big oak barrel on a small two-wheeled cart pulled by a bony old brown mare.

This story's season, light and colours: A blustery, rain-washed late spring: a stormy blue-black night at the start, then fresh leaf-green birches, apple blossom and tulips at the Manor Farm, and dusty, sunny country roads by day. Many of the tricks happen at dusk or at night, in deep indigo moonlight with warm amber lantern and candle glow, and the mornings come up rosy pink. Accent colours: the thief's bottle-green, brass and blossom pink.

The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm, with a goose house full of white geese and a long stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses with cream-and-black manes; he himself rides a big dapple-grey horse. The priest lives at the vicarage, with a huge old linden tree in the garden. The master thief's sack is a big patched brown sack, and the barrel is a big oak barrel on a small two-wheeled cart pulled by a bony old brown mare.

Accent colours: the thief's bottle-green, brass and blossom pink.

Så ble det bryllup. Det var presten som giftet dem. Han hadde fått igjen gullet og sølvet sitt, hver eneste skje, men han så seg over skulderen hver gang han hørte ei gås. Husmannen satt øverst ved bordet i ny frakk, og den gamle kona fra røverhuset danset så hodetørkleet flagret.

Så ble det bryllup, og den gamle kona danset så hodetørkleet flagret.

Alt: Mestertyven og amtmannens datter holder hverandre i hånda i bryllupet på gårdsplassen. Presten ser seg over skulderen etter gjessene, faren sitter øverst ved bordet, og den gamle kona danser.

A merry wedding feast in the sunny yard of the Manor Farm, with a long table full of food under garlands of birch leaves and flowers. In the middle, the Master Thief and the Bailiff's Daughter, wearing a small silver bridal crown, stand hand in hand and laugh as the Priest blesses them, though he glances nervously over his shoulder at two white geese waddling past. At the head of the table sits the Cottager, proud in a smart new dark-blue coat, and in front of the table the Old Woman dances a lively jig, her checked headscarf fluttering.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: A merry wedding feast in the sunny yard of the Manor Farm, with a long table full of food under garlands of birch leaves and flowers. In the middle, the Master Thief and the Bailiff's Daughter, wearing a small silver bridal crown, stand hand in hand and laugh as the Priest blesses them, though he glances nervously over his shoulder at two white geese waddling past. At the head of the table sits the Cottager, proud in a smart new dark-blue coat, and in front of the table the Old Woman dances a lively jig, her checked headscarf fluttering.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Master Thief: A slim, nimble young man of about twenty with a narrow, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey felt hat with a narrow brim, always worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, patched bottle-green coat with deep pockets over a cream shirt, a red neckerchief, narrow charcoal trousers and soft black boots.
- the Bailiff's Daughter: A kind, clever young woman of about nineteen with a heart-shaped face, a dimple in one cheek, lively grey-green eyes that always seem to be laughing, a small straight nose and nut-brown hair in two braids coiled into round buns over her ears. She wears a long apricot-coloured dress with a white embroidered collar and puffed sleeves, and a sprig of white lily of the valley pinned at her collar.
- the Priest: A tall, stiff, very proud priest of about fifty with a long thin face, a long pointed nose held high, raised eyebrows, a small pursed mouth and a long, pointed sandy-grey beard. He wears a round, wide-brimmed black hat, a long black cassock buttoned to the chin, a big white pleated millstone ruff around his neck and black buckled shoes, and clasps a small black hymn book to his chest.
- the Cottager: A thin, timid old cottager of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare, patched mouse-brown smock tied with a cord, baggy patched trousers and old clogs, with a worn grey-and-blue striped blanket wrapped round his shoulders like a shawl.
- the Old Woman: A short, round, jolly old woman of about seventy with bright red apple cheeks, a button nose, twinkling blue eyes, deep laugh lines and wisps of white hair escaping from a red-and-white checked headscarf tied under her chin. She wears a long dark-brown wool dress with the sleeves pushed up, a wide sunflower-yellow apron with a big pocket and sturdy clogs, and keeps a big wooden ladle tucked into her apron strings.

Setting:
- the Manor Farm: A large, prosperous farm around a big grassy yard with a stone well. On one side stands a grand two-storey manor house of white-painted timber with a dark hipped roof, rows of small-paned windows with green shutters, a carved front porch and a bed of red and yellow tulips under the upstairs windows. Around the yard stand a long red stable, a small red goose house and a kitchen wing, with blossoming apple trees and birches behind.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The cottager's tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut stands alone at the edge of the woods. Deep in a dark spruce forest lies the robbers' big, dim timber house with a stone fireplace. The farmer walks his three oxen, big and gentle, reddish-brown with white faces and short curved horns, along the Forest Road. The Bailiff lives at the Manor Farm, with a goose house full of white geese and a long stable of twelve stalls for his twelve dun fjord horses with cream-and-black manes; he himself rides a big dapple-grey horse. The priest lives at the vicarage, with a huge old linden tree in the garden. The master thief's sack is a big patched brown sack, and the barrel is a big oak barrel on a small two-wheeled cart pulled by a bony old brown mare.

This story's season, light and colours: A blustery, rain-washed late spring: a stormy blue-black night at the start, then fresh leaf-green birches, apple blossom and tulips at the Manor Farm, and dusty, sunny country roads by day. Many of the tricks happen at dusk or at night, in deep indigo moonlight with warm amber lantern and candle glow, and the mornings come up rosy pink. Accent colours: the thief's bottle-green, brass and blossom pink.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Tripp, tripp, tripp! Hanen løper så fort han kan.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Rooster: A proud, sturdy farmyard rooster, snow-white all over with glossy white feathers, a big, floppy, bright red comb, red wattles, a short yellow beak, round, earnest black eyes, strong yellow legs with little spurs and a tall, arching tail of long white plumes. He carries himself very upright with his chest puffed out, full of courage, and runs with his wings half spread.

Setting:
- the Nut Wood: A sunny little wood of tall, many-stemmed hazel bushes heavy with clusters of ripe brown hazelnuts in papery husks, with butter-yellow leaves drifting down, a soft carpet of emerald moss scattered with fallen leaves and nutshells, a few mossy grey stones, and a narrow winding path leading out between the bushes towards open fields.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in the countryside around the Nut Wood, a sunny little wood of hazel bushes heavy with ripe hazelnuts. A winding path leads out of the wood to a small bubbling spring with a huge old linden tree on the grassy bank just above it, and from there on to the Virgin Mary's little cottage, the farms and barns of a village, a woodpile at the edge of the spruce forest, a smithy and, deep in the forest, the charcoal burner's clearing with its smoking charcoal stack. The red gold ribbons are shiny red silk ribbons with gold edges, wound on wooden spools. The little wooden bowl is a small, round birchwood bowl.

This story's season, light and colours: Golden October on a clear, crisp day: hazel leaves turned butter-yellow and drifting down, ripe brown hazelnuts, russet bracken and emerald moss under a deep-blue sky, in low, bright sunshine with long shadows. Accents: the rooster's red comb, the red-and-gold ribbons and the Virgin Mary's light blue. In the charcoal burner's clearing: soft blue-grey smoke.

Characters

Hanen hanen · the Rooster

En omsorgsfull og modig hane som ikke gir opp før han har funnet hjelp til Høna.

A proud, sturdy farmyard rooster, snow-white all over with glossy white feathers, a big, floppy, bright red comb, red wattles, a short yellow beak, round, earnest black eyes, strong yellow legs with little spurs and a tall, arching tail of long white plumes. He carries himself very upright with his chest puffed out, full of courage, and runs with his wings half spread.

Høna (Tuppen) hona-tuppen · the Hen

Hanen sin beste venn som får et nøtteskall i halsen, men blir raskt bedre når hun får vann.

A small, round, plump little hen, speckled grey all over with tiny white and charcoal flecks like salt and pepper, with a small neat red comb, a short pale beak, bright round orange eyes, soft fluffy grey feathers on her legs and little grey feet. She has a cheerful, curious, nut-loving look.

Kilden kilden · the Gurgling Spring

En klar, vennlig liten kilde som gir vann når den får friske blader.

A small, round, crystal-clear spring welling up in a ring of mossy grey stones, about as wide as a cartwheel, fringed with ferns and blue forget-me-nots. On its gently bubbling surface a friendly face shows in the ripples: two round, shining bubble eyes and a wide, gurgling mouth. The water is so clear that the pebbles on the bottom sparkle.

Linden linden · the Linden Tree

Et stort og snilt lindetre som gir grønne blader når det får røde gullbånd.

An enormous, ancient linden tree with a broad, rounded crown of heart-shaped leaves just turning from green to gold, a thick, gnarled grey-brown trunk and big roots like knobbly toes. In the bark of the trunk is a kind, sleepy old face: two knot-hole eyes under mossy bark eyebrows, a round knobbly nose and a wide, gentle mouth. Two low branches bend like arms.

Jomfru Maria jomfru-maria · the Virgin Mary

En mild hjelper som gir røde gullbånd når hun får et par sko.

A small, soft, grandmotherly woman of about seventy with a round, kind, wrinkly face, twinkling light-grey eyes, a sweet smile and silver hair under a simple white linen veil. She wears a light-blue knitted shawl over a plain, long lavender dress, and on her feet only darned grey woollen socks, because she has no shoes. She looks like an ordinary kind grandmother, with no halo.

Characters

Kona kona · the Wife

En sta og impulsiv, men godhjertet kone som lett lar seg rive med og ender i små, rare situasjoner.

A cheerful, dreamy farm wife of about forty-five, a little round, with a long ski-jump nose, big round blue eyes that always look amazed, rosy cheeks, a pleased little smile and two long, thin straw-yellow plaits tied at the ends with red wool. She wears a rust-orange wool skirt, a black bodice laced with red ribbon over a white blouse with wide sleeves, wooden-soled shoes and a big white apron with one deep front pocket.

Kona med fjærene kona-med-fjaer · the Feathered Wife

Kona etter slakterens rampestrek: full av tjæreprikker og fjær, så hun tror hun er blitt en stor, rar fugl.

The Wife after the Butcher's prank: the same cheerful woman of about forty-five with a long ski-jump nose, big round amazed blue eyes and two long straw-yellow plaits tied with red wool, in her rust-orange skirt, black laced bodice and white apron, but now covered from head to toe with round black tar dots and fluffy white, grey and brown feathers stuck to her clothes, arms, hair and cheeks, so that she looks like a big, ruffled bird.

Mannen mannen · the Husband

En tålmodig bonde som blir oppgitt, men forsøker å finne trøst i at andre også gjør merkelige ting.

A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a narrow, clever face, a long straight nose, lively dark eyes with laugh crinkles, a patient half-smile, a short, neat black beard and cropped black hair. He wears a small black cap with a turned-up brim, a faded cornflower-blue coat with big pockets and brass buttons, and patched grey trousers tucked into worn brown boots.

Slakteren slakteren · the Butcher

En listig, men ikke skummel handelsmann som finner på en ufarlig rampestrek og får alt til å virke enda rarere.

A huge, barrel-chested butcher of about fifty with a round, shiny red face, a bulbous nose, twinkling little black eyes, bushy black eyebrows, a sly grin and a big, round, bushy black beard. He wears a small white linen cap, a red shirt with the sleeves rolled up over thick arms and a long white apron with blue stripes, and he always has a string of sausages slung over one shoulder.

Kona som vil bære inn sola kona-som-vil-bare-inn-sola · the Sieve Wife

En ivrig husmor som tror hun må bære solskinn inn i et nytt hus og blir overlykkelig når hun får en enkel løsning.

A tiny, quick, bird-like young wife of about twenty-two, hardly taller than a ten-year-old, with a small round face, a pointed chin, bright eager green eyes, rosy cheeks and a mass of glossy black curls tied up in a sunflower-yellow kerchief. She wears an apricot-orange dress with a white apron and red shoes, and she always carries a big, round, shallow wooden sieve with a bottom full of tiny holes.

Den nysgjerrige gårdskona den-nysgjerrige-gardskona · the Curious Farm Wife

En pratsom og godtroende kone som misforstår hvor den reisende er fra og vil sende gaver til den døde mannen sin i himmelen.

A tall, big, well-fed farm wife of about sixty with a large round face, a double chin, pink cheeks, a big mouth always open to talk, bright little inquisitive eyes and iron-grey ringlets under a large round black bonnet trimmed with lace and tied under her chins. She wears a wine-red wool dress with silver buttons and a green silk shawl, and she always holds a long brass ear trumpet to one ear.

Per nummer tre per · Per

Gårdskonas tredje mann, en gretten bonde som blir lurt av mannen fra Ringerike, men som heller dikter opp en historie enn å innrømme det.

A tall, heavy, grumpy farmer of about fifty with a long, sour face, a drooping lower lip, a big red nose, deep frown lines, bristly black eyebrows and a short, stiff iron-grey beard like a doormat. He wears a floppy black stocking cap, a patched leather jerkin over a rust-red shirt, brown knee breeches and tall muddy boots.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: In the warm, firelit farmhouse kitchen, Pål sits at the long table with a big bowl of sour-cream porridge shining with butter, sugar and cinnamon, licking his wooden spoon with his eyes closed in bliss. The Wife stands beside him with her hands clasped, glowing with pride. Outside the small-paned window behind them, the Servant Boy peeks in over the sill with wide eyes, seeing everything.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Pål: A soft, round-bellied young man of about twenty-five, shorter than most, with a round, pale, clean-shaven face, plump pink cheeks, a small upturned nose, big, droopy brown eyes and wavy light-brown hair combed into a proud swoop over his forehead. He wears a short brown jacket over a tight lemon-yellow waistcoat with shiny buttons straining over his tummy, a big floppy pink silk bow at his neck, grey trousers and polished black shoes, and a wooden spoon always sticks out of his breast pocket.
- the Wife: A pretty, lively farm wife of about thirty-five, of medium height, with a round, dimpled face, a small pointed nose, bright dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows and wheat-blonde hair in a thick braid coiled at the back of her head with a red ribbon. She wears a sky-blue laced bodice over a pale-yellow blouse with puffed sleeves, a long red-and-white striped skirt, a big white apron and a string of red glass beads around her neck.
- the Servant Boy: A very skinny, quick farm boy of about thirteen with a mousy-brown pudding-bowl haircut, a narrow, sunburnt face with a pointed chin, a wide, sly grin and quick green eyes that miss nothing. He wears a baggy, faded brick-red shirt and patched brown trousers that are too short for him, so his bony ankles show, and he goes barefoot. His round grey-green knitted cap with a little pompom on top is always either on his head or waving in his hand.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. A small farm on a green hillside: the farmhouse is a dark log house with a grass roof, a stone doorstep and small-paned windows; across the yard stand Pål's smaller, crooked log cottage, the other house, and a big grey barn with a wide double door. Below them a meadow slopes down past a half-built fence of slanting grey poles to Pål's brown field, a little brook and a birch hill. The farmhouse kitchen has a long scrubbed table with benches, an open hearth with a black pot, and a plank door that opens inwards, with room to hide behind it. Rømmegrøt is thick, creamy-white sour-cream porridge in a big round wooden bowl, with a golden pool of melted butter in the middle and cinnamon sugar on top. Lefse is a big, round, thin, soft flatbread.

This story's season, light and colours: Late spring at ploughing time: rich chocolate-brown ploughed earth, birches in bright lime-green new leaf, golden marsh marigolds along the brook, and warm, still sunshine under a clear sky. Indoors: warm hearth firelight and the creamy white of the porridge.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. A grassy track leads from the hut down into the birch forest. Her animals are exactly two white goats, three woolly white sheep and two brown-and-white cows. Her butter churn is a tall, narrow wooden churn with dark hoops and a long wooden dasher sticking out of its lid. The wolf and the fox are natural animals, apart from the fox's little pouch.

The evening scene glows orange and rose over the mountains. Accents: dwarf-birch red, the fox's golden orange and creamy white.

Rike Per Kremmer rigeper · 18/18 pictures

Møllergutten må hente tre fjær fra halen til Dragen ved Dybenfart.

Alt: Møllergutten lister seg forbi den store, sovende dragen med fingeren foran munnen. Dragehalen med tre skinnende gullfjær ligger i en bue på gulvet foran ham.

At night in the Castle Hall, the Miller's Boy tiptoes past the enormous Dragon, who sleeps in his huge four-poster bed, snoring, with a little puff of smoke curling from his nostrils. The Dragon's long tail hangs out of the bed and curls across the floor in the foreground, ending in three long, shining golden feathers. The Miller's Boy looks at the feathers with a finger on his lips and a cheeky, hopeful smile. The fire glows orange.
