The Dragon's long tail hangs out of the bed and curls across the floor in the foreground, ending in three long, shining golden feathers. The Miller's Boy looks at the feathers with a finger on his lips and a cheeky, hopeful smile. The fire glows orange.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Miller's Boy: A sturdy, slightly plump, good-natured lad of about sixteen with a round, open face, a button nose, friendly light-blue eyes, a wide, warm smile and short, curly strawberry-blond hair. He wears a floppy, wide-brimmed grey felt hat with a broad red hatband, a loose white linen shirt, a white miller's apron tied over brown knee breeches, grey stockings and wooden clogs, with a light dusting of flour on his sleeves and hat.
- the Dragon: An enormous, pot-bellied dragon about four times as tall as a man, with bumpy plum-purple scales, a pale lavender belly, short thick legs with big blunt claws, small leathery wings that look far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils that puff little grey smoke clouds, big sleepy amber eyes under heavy lids, and a row of soft orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Setting:
- the Castle Hall: A huge, gloomy hall in an old stone castle, with rough slate-grey walls, a high vaulted ceiling, tall narrow arched windows and grey flagstone floors. A big stone fireplace glows with embers. On one side stands an enormous, dragon-sized four-poster bed with a rumpled plum-coloured quilt, and beside it a small, plain bed. A huge old two-handed sword hangs on iron hooks on the wall, above a long table and bench.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. Rich Per Kremmer lives on a big, prosperous farm; just below it a little grey watermill turns on a brook, and far downstream on the river stands a second, older mill with a big wooden waterwheel. The little chest is a small pine box painted with blue and red rosemaling flowers, with an iron key in its lock. Per's letters are folded papers sealed with red wax. The robbers' farm is a shabby log farmhouse deep in a dark spruce forest. At a wide river far away waits the old ferry: a long, flat-bottomed, tarred black punt with square ends, pushed with a very long wooden pole. On the hill beyond it stands the Dragon's crooked, slate-grey stone castle at Dybenfart. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers, each as long as a man's arm.

This story's season, light and colours: Late spring along the rivers: fast, high, glittering water, bird-cherry trees foaming with white blossom on the banks, marsh marigolds glowing yellow in the wet meadows, and long rosy-gold sunsets. At night: deep blue shadows and warm lamplight. Inside the Dragon's castle: slate-blue gloom and ember-orange firelight.

Characters

Møllergutten mollergutten · the Miller's Boy

En modig, høflig og snill gutt som møter mange farer uten å miste hjertet sitt, og som til slutt skaper et godt liv for seg og den han elsker.

A sturdy, slightly plump, good-natured lad of about sixteen with a round, open face, a button nose, friendly light-blue eyes, a wide, warm smile and short, curly strawberry-blond hair. He wears a floppy, wide-brimmed grey felt hat with a broad red hatband, a loose white linen shirt, a white miller's apron tied over brown knee breeches, grey stockings and wooden clogs, with a light dusting of flour on his sleeves and hat.

Rike Per Kremmer rike-per-kremmer · Rich Per

En svært rik, sta handelsmann som vil styre alt, men som lærer at det ikke lønner seg å være grådig og slem.

A tall, bony merchant of about fifty with a long, horsey face, a jutting chin, a sharp hooked nose, small, darting, greedy grey eyes, a thin mouth, bushy salt-and-pepper side-whiskers and slicked-back black hair with a pointed widow's peak. He wears a long wine-red frock coat whose big pockets bulge with rolls of coloured ribbon, a shiny green-and-gold striped silk waistcoat, grey knee breeches, white stockings and buckled shoes, a gold ring on every finger and a fat leather money purse on his belt.

Pers datter pers-datter · Per's Daughter

En rolig og vennlig ung kvinne som blir behandlet som en premie, men som ender med et liv der godhet og samarbeid betyr mer enn penger.

A kind, soft-spoken young woman of about eighteen, tall and willowy, with a long neck, a narrow face with a delicate chin, a small straight nose, soft brown eyes under pale brows, pink cheeks, and thick auburn hair in one long plait reaching her waist, tied with a white ribbon. She wears a midnight-blue wool dress with a band of red-and-white woven trim at the hem and cuffs, and a round silver brooch at her collar.

Prinsessa ved Dybenfart prinsessa-ved-dybenfart · the Princess

En klok prinsesse som hjelper møllergutten med list og mot, og som endelig får reise hjem.

A small, quick-witted princess of about twenty with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small straight nose, bright dark eyes that miss nothing and a wry, lopsided smile. Her dark hair is cut short in a cap of springy curls, held back by a thin silver band set with one pearl. She wears a long turquoise gown with wide bell sleeves, a silver-embroidered belt and soft grey slippers.

Dragen ved Dybenfart dragen · the Dragon

En diger, gretten drage med tre skinnende gullfjær ytterst på halen. Han liker ikke fremmede folk, og han vil helst få sove i fred.

An enormous, pot-bellied dragon about four times as tall as a man, with bumpy plum-purple scales, a pale lavender belly, short thick legs with big blunt claws, small leathery wings that look far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils that puff little grey smoke clouds, big sleepy amber eyes under heavy lids, and a row of soft orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Ferjemannen ferjemannen · the Old Ferryman

En krokrygget gubbe som har staket folk over den brede elva i hundre år, og som gjerne vil bli fri.

A tiny, wiry, very old man, bent almost double like a fish hook, with a wrinkled nut-brown face, a sharp little beak of a nose, bright little black eyes twinkling under bushy snow-white eyebrows, a toothless grin and no beard, and thin white hair tied at the back in a stubby little pigtail. He wears a battered, wide-brimmed straw hat, a faded sea-green smock with patched elbows and rolled-up grey trousers, goes barefoot on knobbly feet and always holds a very long wooden punting pole.

- the Miller's Boy: A sturdy, slightly plump, good-natured lad of about sixteen with a round, open face, a button nose, friendly light-blue eyes, a wide, warm smile and short, curly strawberry-blond hair. He wears a floppy, wide-brimmed grey felt hat with a broad red hatband, a loose white linen shirt, a white miller's apron tied over brown knee breeches, grey stockings and wooden clogs, with a light dusting of flour on his sleeves and hat.
- Per's Daughter: A kind, soft-spoken young woman of about eighteen, tall and willowy, with a long neck, a narrow face with a delicate chin, a small straight nose, soft brown eyes under pale brows, pink cheeks, and thick auburn hair in one long plait reaching her waist, tied with a white ribbon. She wears a midnight-blue wool dress with a band of red-and-white woven trim at the hem and cuffs, and a round silver brooch at her collar.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. Rich Per Kremmer lives on a big, prosperous farm; just below it a little grey watermill turns on a brook, and far downstream on the river stands a second, older mill with a big wooden waterwheel. The little chest is a small pine box painted with blue and red rosemaling flowers, with an iron key in its lock. Per's letters are folded papers sealed with red wax. The robbers' farm is a shabby log farmhouse deep in a dark spruce forest. At a wide river far away waits the old ferry: a long, flat-bottomed, tarred black punt with square ends, pushed with a very long wooden pole. On the hill beyond it stands the Dragon's crooked, slate-grey stone castle at Dybenfart. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers, each as long as a man's arm.

This story's season, light and colours: Late spring along the rivers: fast, high, glittering water, bird-cherry trees foaming with white blossom on the banks, marsh marigolds glowing yellow in the wet meadows, and long rosy-gold sunsets. At night: deep blue shadows and warm lamplight. Inside the Dragon's castle: slate-blue gloom and ember-orange firelight.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Devil: A small, pot-bellied devil about as tall as a seven-year-old child, with shiny tomato-red skin, a round face with a button nose, big goggly amber eyes, pointy ears, a long, pointed black goatee and two big black ram's horns curling out of his forehead. He has a very long, thin tail with an arrow-shaped tip and little black goat hooves. He wears a smart soot-black waistcoat with shiny brass buttons stretched over his tummy. Vain, boastful and silly, never scary.
- the Smith: A tall, long-legged blacksmith of about forty with a broad barrel chest and thick, strong forearms, a long, cocky face with a jutting chin, a big bumpy nose, twinkling hazel eyes, a chestnut-brown handlebar moustache curled up at both ends and short chestnut hair that sticks straight up like a brush. Setting:
- the Smithy Yard: Outside the smithy: a squat, soot-blackened log building with a grass-covered turf roof, a crooked stone chimney and wide double doors, beside a dusty ochre country road with dry grassy verges. A gnarled old pear tree heavy with ripe yellow pears grows against its sunny side wall over sun-dried grass, with a split-rail fence behind. Parched, straw-yellow hay meadows with haystacks and a few birches in the distance.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The smith's smithy is a squat log building with a grass-covered turf roof, soot-blackened walls and wide double doors, standing beside a dusty country road. The wire purse is a small, round coin purse of woven silver-grey steel wire, the size of a child's hand, with a snap clasp. The smith's big hammer is a heavy iron sledgehammer with a long ash handle. Far along the road, the way splits in two: one road climbs a green hill into soft white clouds to the gate of heaven, a tall arched gate of white-painted wood with gold hinges; the other dips into a smoky, rocky gully to the Devil's gate, a tall, crooked, soot-black iron gate with nine big iron locks in a row and one huge padlock.

This story's season, light and colours: A heatwave in the hottest days of summer: glaring white-gold sunlight, parched straw-yellow grass, an ochre dust road shimmering in the heat and ripe yellow pears among dusty green leaves. Inside the smithy: soot-black and charcoal greys lit by glowing ember-orange and showers of bright sparks. At the gate of heaven: soft white clouds and pale gold light; at the Devil's gate: a smoky plum-purple haze.

- Halvor: A tall, lanky lad of about eighteen with a lazy slouch, a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy half-closed hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead. He wears a ragged, soot-streaked grey wool shirt with holes at the elbows, baggy patched brown trousers held up with a piece of rope, and battered brown shoes, with a charred poking stick tucked into the rope.

Story world: Old Norway, long ago. Halvor's home is a tiny, poor turf-roofed log cottage on a hillside above the sea, with one low room, a big open stone hearth full of ashes and not a single chair. Far across the sea lies an empty green land where three troll castles stand far apart, each grander than the last, with light in every window. The troll sword in each castle is a big old sword with a plain iron hilt; the magic bottle is a small green glass bottle with a cork. The wishing ring is a chunky silver ring with one round blue stone; the ring left in its place is a small, plain gold band. The magic boots are cracked old brown leather boots. Halvor's horse is a skinny, shaggy dun horse with a drooping head. Soria Moria is a castle of glittering golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

This story's season, light and colours: Early autumn, mostly long blue dusks and clear moonlit nights: deep ultramarine and indigo skies, silver moonlight, violet-blue shadows and warm golden light glittering from castle windows far away. Indoors, amber firelight gleams on gold and silver. Daylight is cool and silvery. Accents: the youngest princess's red and the rose-and-ember glow of the sunset over Halvor's home.

Halvor i fine klær halvor-fine · Halvor in Fine Clothes

Halvor etter at prinsessene har gitt ham klær så fine at han kunne vært en kongssønn.

A tall, lanky lad of about eighteen with a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy hazel eyes, a lopsided smile and messy auburn hair, now washed clean and dressed like a king's son: a royal-blue velvet coat with gold buttons and gold-embroidered cuffs, a white linen shirt with a frilled collar, a wide lingonberry-red sash, cream breeches, white stockings and shiny black buckled shoes.

Den eldste prinsessa eldest-princess · the Eldest Princess

Den eldste av de tre prinsessene. Hun sitter ved rokken i det første slottet og liker å ha det ryddig.

A tall, stately princess of about twenty-four with warm golden-brown skin, a long oval face, a straight nose, calm dark-brown eyes, neat arched eyebrows and thick black hair coiled into two round buns over her ears. She wears a small gold crown, a long plum-purple velvet dress with a high collar and long sleeves, and a crisp white apron with a lace edge, because she likes everything tidy.

Den mellomste prinsessa middle-princess · the Middle Princess

Den mellomste av de tre prinsessene, som blir så glad når trollet er borte at hun ikke vet hvilket bein hun skal stå på.

A short, bouncy princess of about twenty-one with warm golden-brown skin, a round face with dimpled cheeks, a small button nose, merry black eyes and glossy black hair cut in a thick, chin-length bob with a straight fringe. She wears a small gold crown, a long sunflower-yellow dress with puffed sleeves and a wide white sash, and a necklace of big white pearls.

Den yngste prinsessa youngest-princess · the Youngest Princess

Den yngste og vakreste av de tre prinsessene, som gir Halvor en ønskering og ber ham aldri si et ord om dem.

A graceful, slender princess of about eighteen with warm golden-brown skin, a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large, bright dark-brown eyes with long lashes, a warm smile and long, straight, glossy black hair falling loose to her waist. She wears a small gold crown, a long red dress with a square neckline and wide bell sleeves edged with gold braid, and a tiny gold sun pendant on a thin chain.

Trollet med tre hoder three-headed-troll · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet i det første slottet, som snuser med alle tre nesene og brøler «Huttetu!», men går opp i en liten, grå sky når Halvor svinger sverdet.

A big, pear-shaped troll about twice as tall as a man, with blue-grey, knobbly skin, long dangling arms and huge flat feet. He has exactly three heads side by side on his broad shoulders, each with a big round nose: the left head is sleepy, with droopy eyelids and a floppy red nightcap; the middle head is grumpy, with one bushy black eyebrow; the right head is surprised, with round eyes and a tuft of white hair. He wears a patched brown leather jerkin tied with rope.

Trollet med seks hoder six-headed-troll · the Six-Headed Troll

Trollet i det andre slottet. Han er så stor at han må snu seg sidelengs for å komme inn døra, men PUFF! sier han likevel.

A huge, barrel-shaped troll about three times as tall as a man, with pale sandstone-yellow skin covered in brown freckles and warts, and shoulders so wide that he must turn sideways to get through doors. He has exactly six heads in one long row along his shoulders, each with a long pointed nose, small beady eyes and a stiff tuft of black hair. He wears a huge patchwork coat sewn from old sacks and goes barefoot.

Trollet med ni hoder nine-headed-troll · the Nine-Headed Troll

Det største og seigeste trollet, i det tredje slottet. Han blir blekere og blekere for hver SVISJ, helt til han går opp i en stor, grå sky.

An enormous troll as tall as a house, the biggest of all, with dark charcoal-grey skin, rough and lumpy like wet rock, a round belly and thick, stumpy legs. He has exactly nine small, round heads on short, thick necks, spread out in a wide fan above his shoulders, each with a potato nose, bushy white eyebrows and a wide, frog-like mouth. He wears a ragged sheepskin cloak and a belt of knotted rope.

Mor mother · the Mother

Halvors mor, som ler så hun må holde seg på magen, og som kjenner igjen gutten sin når ilden blusser opp.

A small, sturdy, quick-moving woman of about fifty with a round chin, a wide mouth made for laughing, a little upturned nose, bright brown eyes and dark-brown hair streaked with grey, tucked under a faded indigo headscarf knotted on top of her head. She wears a patched heather-purple wool dress with rolled-up sleeves, a faded green apron and wooden clogs.

Far father · the Father

Halvors far, en stille mann som ser inn i ilden og savner gutten sin.

A broad, slow-moving, heavy-set man of about sixty with a big round face, ruddy cheeks, a bulbous nose, a bushy salt-and-pepper beard and a bald head under a knitted blue cap. He wears a worn moss-green wool jacket over a collarless linen shirt, patched brown knee breeches, grey knitted stockings and heavy leather boots.

Kona med den lange nesa old-cottage-woman · the Old Woman

Ei gammel kone med ei nese så lang at hun roter i glørne med den, som spør månen og vestavinden om veien til Soria Moria og gir Halvor et par støvler for hesten hans.

A tall, bony, very old woman with a long thin neck, knobbly hands, a wrinkled, cheerful face, small twinkling black eyes and an enormously long, thin, pointed nose with a rosy tip, as long as a wooden spoon, which she uses to poke the embers. Her dove-grey hair peeps out in wisps from under a white linen cap. She wears a faded heather-blue wool dress, a black apron and wooden clogs.

Vestavinden west-wind · the West Wind

En travel vind som suser inn over skogen på vei til Soria Moria for å tørke bryllupsklærne, og som lar Halvor henge på så godt han kan.

A friendly wind spirit the size of a big man, with a round, rosy, beardless face, a wide merry grin and bright green eyes. His wild, streaming hair is made of whirling leaves and spruce needles, with three wooden clothes-pegs clipped in it, because he dries the washing. From the chest down his body turns into long, curling swirls of misty sea-green and silver air with leaves spinning inside, and he has long, thin, windy arms.

Story world: Old Norway, long ago. Halvor's home is a tiny, poor turf-roofed log cottage on a hillside above the sea, with one low room, a big open stone hearth full of ashes and not a single chair. Far across the sea lies an empty green land where three troll castles stand far apart, each grander than the last, with light in every window. The troll sword in each castle is a big old sword with a plain iron hilt; the magic bottle is a small green glass bottle with a cork. The wishing ring is a chunky silver ring with one round blue stone; the ring left in its place is a small, plain gold band. The magic boots are cracked old brown leather boots. Halvor's horse is a skinny, shaggy dun horse with a drooping head. Soria Moria is a castle of glittering golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

This story's season, light and colours: Early autumn, mostly long blue dusks and clear moonlit nights: deep ultramarine and indigo skies, silver moonlight, violet-blue shadows and warm golden light glittering from castle windows far away. Indoors, amber firelight gleams on gold and silver. Daylight is cool and silvery. Accents: the youngest princess's red and the rose-and-ember glow of the sunset over Halvor's home.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

The troll sword in each castle is a big old sword with a plain iron hilt; the magic bottle is a small green glass bottle with a cork. The wishing ring is a chunky silver ring with one round blue stone; the ring left in its place is a small, plain gold band. The magic boots are cracked old brown leather boots. Halvor's horse is a skinny, shaggy dun horse with a drooping head. Soria Moria is a castle of glittering golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

This story's season, light and colours: Early autumn, mostly long blue dusks and clear moonlit nights: deep ultramarine and indigo skies, silver moonlight, violet-blue shadows and warm golden light glittering from castle windows far away. Indoors, amber firelight gleams on gold and silver. Daylight is cool and silvery. Accents: the youngest princess's red and the rose-and-ember glow of the sunset over Halvor's home.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Å, det ville gutten gjerne. Han la seg ned med hodet i fanget hennes. Hun klødde og spant, og spant og klødde. Langt borte fór føllene mellom trærne som lyse streker. Men det så ikke gutten. Han sov.

Hun klør og spinner, og spinner og klør. Og gutten sover.

Alt: Den eldste broren sover med hodet i fanget til en bitte liten, gammel kone i ei hule i berget. Hun spinner og klør ham i håret, mens føllene suser forbi langt borte.

At the old woman's rock cleft, a small cave at the foot of a grey cliff, the Old Woman sits at her little spinning wheel, spinning with one hand and scratching the hair of the Eldest Brother with the other. He lies stretched out with his head in her lap, fast asleep with his mouth open, his straw hat fallen off. Far away between the birch trees, the seven foals flash past like bright streaks. Warm midday light and soft shadows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Old Woman: A tiny, hunched old woman, no taller than a ten-year-old child, with a small, wrinkled face, a very long, pointed nose that nearly touches her chin, little twinkling black eyes, a sweet, sly smile and wisps of white hair. She is wrapped in many layered shawls of faded blue, brown, plum and grey, one on top of the other, over a long dark skirt, with worn felt slippers on her feet.
- the Eldest Brother: A tall, gawky lad of about nineteen with a long, bony face, a big chin, heavy-lidded sleepy eyes, a long nose, a lazy, lopsided grin and thick, wavy dark-blond hair that sticks up at the back. He wears a red-and-white checked shirt with rolled sleeves, baggy brown trousers held up by a single braces strap and a wide, frayed straw hat, and he goes barefoot.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The poor family lives in a tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut deep in a spruce forest. The seven foals are glossy chestnut foals with flaxen manes and tails, all alike except the youngest and smallest, who has a white star on his forehead. As princes they are seven brothers from about ten to twenty, with their sister's strawberry-blonde hair and shining white-and-gold clothes. The old woman's rock cleft is a small, shallow cave at the foot of a grey cliff beside a forest path, with a little spinning wheel inside. A big white birch stump in a clearing hides a door to a small secret room with rough wooden walls, a hearth, a shelf with a small brown jar and a big, rusty sword on a hook. The church is small and black-tarred with a tall tower, beyond a long wooden bridge over a river.

This story's season, light and colours: Midsummer: long, pale-gold days, a low sun that hardly sets and bright, pale nights under a lilac sky; violet mountains on the horizon, purple heather, birch woods and dewy grass, with long golden shadows in the evenings. The wedding glows with warm candlelight and golden light spilling from open doors.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Askeladden tok krukka ned fra hylla og drakk. Glugg. Så en slurk til. Glugg. Og en til. Glugg! Nå løftet han sverdet like lett som en tannbørste.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A sturdy, broad-shouldered boy of about fifteen with full, round, sun-browned cheeks, a short straight nose, calm green eyes, a steady, determined smile and thick sandy-brown hair tied at the back of his neck with a leather cord. He wears a patched rust-orange wool jacket with bone buttons over a cream shirt, dark-green trousers tucked into sturdy black boots, and a small brown leather knapsack on his back.
- the King: A lean, severe king of about sixty, tall and straight-backed, with a long, bony face, stern frown lines, sharp, narrow hazel eyes under bushy black eyebrows and a short, neatly trimmed grey beard. He wears a long dark-red robe with a grey fur collar, a thick gold chain across his chest, a small, spiky gold crown and pointed black shoes.
- the Princess: A cheerful princess of about sixteen with a round, freckled face, warm brown eyes, a wide, happy smile and a mass of bouncy strawberry-blonde curls falling past her shoulders, with a small gold crown set with a green stone. She wears a long pale-green dress with white lace at the collar and cuffs, a gold-embroidered belt and pale-green slippers.
- the Youngest Prince: A small, quick boy prince of about ten, the youngest of seven brothers, with a round, freckled face, big dark eyes, a huge beaming smile and tousled strawberry-blonde hair. He wears shining white-and-gold clothes: a white tunic embroidered with gold, a short white cape with gold trim, white breeches and soft white boots, with a small white star embroidered on the chest of his tunic.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The poor family lives in a tiny, crooked turf-roofed hut deep in a spruce forest. The seven foals are glossy chestnut foals with flaxen manes and tails, all alike except the youngest and smallest, who has a white star on his forehead. As princes they are seven brothers from about ten to twenty, with their sister's strawberry-blonde hair and shining white-and-gold clothes. The old woman's rock cleft is a small, shallow cave at the foot of a grey cliff beside a forest path, with a little spinning wheel inside. A big white birch stump in a clearing hides a door to a small secret room with rough wooden walls, a hearth, a shelf with a small brown jar and a big, rusty sword on a hook. The church is small and black-tarred with a tall tower, beyond a long wooden bridge over a river.

This story's season, light and colours: Midsummer: long, pale-gold days, a low sun that hardly sets and bright, pale nights under a lilac sky; violet mountains on the horizon, purple heather, birch woods and dewy grass, with long golden shadows in the evenings. The wedding glows with warm candlelight and golden light spilling from open doors.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

De tre prinsessene i Hvittenland tentland · 17/17 pictures

Tre prinsesser sitter fast i den hvite sanden i Hvittenland.

Alt: Gutten står på en melkehvit strand og ser forundret på tre prinsessehoder som stikker opp av sanden. Oppe på bakken ligger et grått trollslott, og fra et tårnvindu titter et gult troll med tre hoder.

On the dazzling White Beach under a pale spring sky, the Fisher Lad has just stepped out of his little rowing boat and stares in wonder at three princess heads sticking up out of the milk-white sand in a row: the Eldest Princess, the Middle Princess and the Youngest Princess, who smiles at him. On the hill behind, the gloomy troll castle looms, and the Three-Headed Troll, its three stacked heads grinning, peeks out of a tower window holding three bundles of birch twigs.

Picture: On the dazzling White Beach under a pale spring sky, the Fisher Lad has just stepped out of his little rowing boat and stares in wonder at three princess heads sticking up out of the milk-white sand in a row: the Eldest Princess, the Middle Princess and the Youngest Princess, who smiles at him. On the hill behind, the gloomy troll castle looms, and the Three-Headed Troll, its three stacked heads grinning, peeks out of a tower window holding three bundles of birch twigs.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Fisher Lad: A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about twenty with an open, square face, a strong nose with a small bump, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble on his cheeks and chin. He wears a thick, cream-coloured cable-knit fisherman's sweater, dark-blue canvas trousers rolled up at the ankles and sturdy knee-high sea boots of tan leather, and a red handkerchief with white dots pokes out of his pocket.
- the Eldest Princess: A very tall, thin princess of about twenty-two with a long neck, a narrow, haughty face, a sharp chin, a thin nose turned up at the tip, pale-blue eyes and glossy chocolate-brown hair pulled up into one very high, tight ponytail that swings like a horse's tail. She wears a stiff magenta silk dress with long, pointed hanging sleeves, a gold-trimmed bodice and a very wide skirt, many jingling gold bracelets on both wrists, and a little gold crown tilted to one side.
- the Middle Princess: A small, plump, chatty princess of about twenty with a round, pink face, a wide mouth that hardly ever stops talking, a turned-up nose, big round hazel eyes and a huge, fluffy cloud of carrot-orange curls piled on top of her head with a pink bow. She wears a lime-green dress with white polka dots and three rows of ruffles on the skirt, a pink sash, and a string of big pink beads around her neck.
- the Youngest Princess: A calm, thoughtful princess of about eighteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. A thin silver circlet with one pearl rests on her forehead. She wears a plain sky-blue linen dress with long, close-fitting sleeves, a narrow belt of silver links and a hem sewn with small silver stars, and soft white shoes.
- the Three-Headed Troll: A round, fuzzy troll about twice as tall as a man, with bright mustard-yellow skin covered in short, soft fuzz like a bumblebee, a fat round belly, short arms and huge flat feet. It has exactly three heads stacked on top of one another like a snowman: a big head at the bottom, a middle-sized one and a small one on top, each with a long pink nose, round black eyes and a wide, cheeky grin. It wears baggy, patched brown trousers with braces.

Setting:
- the White Beach: A long, wide beach of sand as smooth and white as fresh milk, beside a calm, pale turquoise sea with tiny waves. A few smooth white pebbles and pale shells lie scattered about, and low white dunes with tufts of silver-grey grass rise behind the beach. Farther inland, on a low hill, stands a gloomy castle of dark grey stone with pointed towers and a big arched gate.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea, long ago. The fisherman's small grey cottage with a turf roof stands on the shore right next to the king's castle, and his boat is a small, tarred, dark-brown rowing boat with two oars. Far across the great sea lies Hvittenland, whose beach is sand as white as milk, with the trolls' gloomy grey castle on a hill behind it and two lions at its gate. The queen's own castle in Hvittenland is white, with a stone stair up to its door. The trolls' birch switches are bundles of thin, bare birch twigs. The queen's wish ring is a plain gold ring, and the little ring she ties into his hair is a tiny gold ring on a blue thread. The magic hat, cloak and boots are a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and a pair of tall brown boots.

This story's season, light and colours: The bright, cold light of early spring in the far north: a copper-red sunset over the sea at the start, then the dazzling milk-white beach of Hvittenland under a pale pearl-blue sky, with turquoise shallows and pale lemon sunrises. The tickling nights happen in near darkness, lit by one warm candle. On the long journey: deep snow still on blue mountains, a steel-grey cold sea and wild, racing storm clouds. Accents: the princess's sky blue and the gold of rings and crowns.

Fiskergutten gutten · the Fisher Lad

Fiskerens sønn, som vokser opp på slottet hos kongen, driver over havet til Hvittenland og holder ut tre netter med trollkiling.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about twenty with an open, square face, a strong nose with a small bump, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble on his cheeks and chin. He wears a thick, cream-coloured cable-knit fisherman's sweater, dark-blue canvas trousers rolled up at the ankles and sturdy knee-high sea boots of tan leather, and a red handkerchief with white dots pokes out of his pocket.

Den unge kongen den-unge-kongen · the Young King

Fiskerens sønn som blir oppdratt på slottet, viser mot og tålmodighet, og legger ut på en lang reise for å finne tilbake til dronningen sin.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered young king of about twenty, a fisherman's son, with an open, square face, a strong nose with a small bump, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble. On his head sits a small, plain gold crown with five points. Over his thick cream cable-knit fisherman's sweater he wears a long white wool cloak edged with silver embroidery of little waves, dark-blue trousers and knee-high boots of tan leather.

Fiskeren fiskeren · the Fisherman

Faren til gutten, en fattig fisker som fisker til kongens bord og lover bort noe han ikke vet hva er.

A lean, wiry fisherman of about forty-five with a long, weather-beaten face, deep laughter lines, a sharp nose, kind, crinkly blue eyes and a long, drooping black moustache, but no beard. On his head sits a round, brimless sealskin cap. He wears a thick grey wool jumper under a long, stiff fishing apron of dark oiled leather, grey trousers tucked into heavy wooden-soled boots, and a coil of fishing line hangs at his belt.

Den gamle mannen ved stranden den-gamle-mannen-ved-stranden · the Old Man

En vennlig veiviser med langt hvitt skjegg som gir gutten viktige råd ved den melkehvite stranden.

A lean, straight-backed old man of about eighty, as bony and long-limbed as a heron, with a long, narrow, sun-browned face, a hooked nose, bright pale-blue eyes under wild white eyebrows and a long white beard braided into one thin plait with a tiny white shell tied at its end. He wears a battered yellow sou'wester hat, a long, faded yellow oilskin coat and tall black sea boots, and leans on a tall, twisted, silver-grey driftwood staff.

Den yngste prinsessen den-yngste-prinsessen · the Youngest Princess

Den kloke og snille prinsessen som gir gode råd, hjelper ham å bryte magien, og savner ham når de blir skilt.

A calm, thoughtful princess of about eighteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. A thin silver circlet with one pearl rests on her forehead. She wears a plain sky-blue linen dress with long, close-fitting sleeves, a narrow belt of silver links and a hem sewn with small silver stars, and soft white shoes.

Dronningen av Hvittenland dronningen · the Queen

Den yngste prinsessen etter bryllupet, nå dronning i Hvittenland. Hun gir den unge kongen en ønskering og knytter en liten ring fast i håret hans.

A calm young queen of about eighteen with a softly rounded chin, a small nose with a slight upturn, sea-grey eyes under soft brows, a quiet, knowing half-smile and long, wavy golden hair that flows down to her waist. On her head sits a tall gold crown set with pale-blue stones. She wears a sky-blue gown with a bodice laced with silver cord and a long train, and a short white fur cape fastened with a round silver clasp.

Den eldste prinsessen eldste-prinsessen · the Eldest Princess

Den eldste av de tre prinsessene som sitter fast i sanden. Hun roper og lokker på gutten.

A very tall, thin princess of about twenty-two with a long neck, a narrow, haughty face, a sharp chin, a thin nose turned up at the tip, pale-blue eyes and glossy chocolate-brown hair pulled up into one very high, tight ponytail that swings like a horse's tail. She wears a stiff magenta silk dress with long, pointed hanging sleeves, a gold-trimmed bodice and a very wide skirt, many jingling gold bracelets on both wrists, and a little gold crown tilted to one side.

Den mellomste prinsessen mellomste-prinsessen · the Middle Princess

Den mellomste av de tre prinsessene som sitter fast i sanden. Hun roper og lokker på gutten, hun også.

A small, plump, chatty princess of about twenty with a round, pink face, a wide mouth that hardly ever stops talking, a turned-up nose, big round hazel eyes and a huge, fluffy cloud of carrot-orange curls piled on top of her head with a pink bow. She wears a lime-green dress with white polka dots and three rows of ruffles on the skirt, a pink sash, and a string of big pink beads around her neck.

Trollet med tre hoder trollet-med-tre-hoder · the Three-Headed Troll

Det første trollet i trollslottet. Det kommer med tre ris og kiler gutten en hel natt.

A round, fuzzy troll about twice as tall as a man, with bright mustard-yellow skin covered in short, soft fuzz like a bumblebee, a fat round belly, short arms and huge flat feet. It has exactly three heads stacked on top of one another like a snowman: a big head at the bottom, a middle-sized one and a small one on top, each with a long pink nose, round black eyes and a wide, cheeky grin. It wears baggy, patched brown trousers with braces.

Trollet med seks hoder trollet-med-seks-hoder · the Six-Headed Troll

Det andre trollet, med seks hoder og seks ris. Det kiler enda verre enn det første.

A tall, lanky troll about three times as tall as a man, with sooty black skin, a big white belly like a puffin's, long thin arms and big orange feet. It has exactly six small, round heads on long, thin necks, three growing from each shoulder like two bunches of flowers; each head has a big, bright orange nose, small white eyes with black dots and a tuft of white hair sticking straight up. It wears a short grey wool kilt.

Trollet med ni hoder trollet-med-ni-hoder · the Nine-Headed Troll

Det største trollet av dem alle, med ni hoder og ni ris. Det kiler lengst og ler høyest.

The biggest troll of all, as tall as a house, with a huge, round, lumpy body of creamy-white skin covered in big chocolate-brown patches like a cow's, stumpy legs and big round hands. It has exactly nine heads growing in a ring around the top of its body like a crown; each head has a wide pink snout, sleepy little brown eyes, floppy ears and a big mouth made for laughing. It wears a huge, patched nightshirt with red-and-white checks.

Nordavinden nordavinden · the North Wind

En kraftig, men hjelpsom vind som lager et bråk ved slottet og rydder veien slik at kongen kan komme inn.

A tall, lean, long-limbed storm giant, three times as tall as a man, with a long, bony, windburnt face, hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, a wide mouth pursed to blow and bright, shining silver eyes. His wild, tangled slate-grey hair and long, wispy beard stream sideways as if in a gale. He wears a huge, billowing cloak made of dark-grey storm clouds, torn into ragged wisps at the edges, and from the knees down he fades into swirling grey mist.

Den gamle gjedda den-gamle-gjedda · the Old Pike

En svært gammel fisk som husker veien til Hvittenland og forteller at dronningen snart skal gifte seg med en annen, så kongen skynder seg videre.

A huge, very old pike as long as a rowing boat, with a long, flat, duck-bill snout, a slightly jutting lower jaw with a kind, closed-mouth smile, and wise, wrinkled golden eyes. Her back is dark olive-green with rows of pale yellow spots, fading to a creamy-white belly, and her fins and tail are ragged and frayed at the edges. Long strands of green waterweed trail from her chin like a thin beard.

Han hoppet ned i båten for å hente det. Og i samme øyeblikk – svisj! – gled båten ut fra land. Helt av seg selv!

Svisj! Båten gled ut fra land. Helt av seg selv!

Alt: Gutten står i robåten med lommetørkleet i hånden og ser seg forskrekket tilbake mens båten glir ut fra land av seg selv. På stranden strekker faren armene etter ham.

Evening at the shore below the king's castle: the Fisher Lad stands in the little rowing boat, holding up his red handkerchief, and looks back in astonishment as the boat glides away from land all by itself, leaving a long silvery trail in the still water. On the stony shore, the Fisherman reaches out after him with both arms, his mouth open in a shout. Dusky blue light and the first stars.

- Image 2: model sheet for the Fisherman, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Fisherman's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Fisherman only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Evening at the shore below the king's castle: the Fisher Lad stands in the little rowing boat, holding up his red handkerchief, and looks back in astonishment as the boat glides away from land all by itself, leaving a long silvery trail in the still water. On the stony shore, the Fisherman reaches out after him with both arms, his mouth open in a shout. Dusky blue light and the first stars.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Fisher Lad: A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about twenty with an open, square face, a strong nose with a small bump, grey-green eyes that crinkle when he laughs, short, wavy brown hair and short brown stubble on his cheeks and chin. He wears a thick, cream-coloured cable-knit fisherman's sweater, dark-blue canvas trousers rolled up at the ankles and sturdy knee-high sea boots of tan leather, and a red handkerchief with white dots pokes out of his pocket.
- the Fisherman: A lean, wiry fisherman of about forty-five with a long, weather-beaten face, deep laughter lines, a sharp nose, kind, crinkly blue eyes and a long, drooping black moustache, but no beard. On his head sits a round, brimless sealskin cap. He wears a thick grey wool jumper under a long, stiff fishing apron of dark oiled leather, grey trousers tucked into heavy wooden-soled boots, and a coil of fishing line hangs at his belt.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea, long ago. The fisherman's small grey cottage with a turf roof stands on the shore right next to the king's castle, and his boat is a small, tarred, dark-brown rowing boat with two oars. Far across the great sea lies Hvittenland, whose beach is sand as white as milk, with the trolls' gloomy grey castle on a hill behind it and two lions at its gate. The queen's own castle in Hvittenland is white, with a stone stair up to its door. The trolls' birch switches are bundles of thin, bare birch twigs. The queen's wish ring is a plain gold ring, and the little ring she ties into his hair is a tiny gold ring on a blue thread. The magic hat, cloak and boots are a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and a pair of tall brown boots.

This story's season, light and colours: The bright, cold light of early spring in the far north: a copper-red sunset over the sea at the start, then the dazzling milk-white beach of Hvittenland under a pale pearl-blue sky, with turquoise shallows and pale lemon sunrises. The tickling nights happen in near darkness, lit by one warm candle. On the long journey: deep snow still on blue mountains, a steel-grey cold sea and wild, racing storm clouds. Accents: the princess's sky blue and the gold of rings and crowns.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

On his head sits a small, plain gold crown with five points. Over his thick cream cable-knit fisherman's sweater he wears a long white wool cloak edged with silver embroidery of little waves, dark-blue trousers and knee-high boots of tan leather.
- the North Wind: A tall, lean, long-limbed storm giant, three times as tall as a man, with a long, bony, windburnt face, hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, a wide mouth pursed to blow and bright, shining silver eyes. His wild, tangled slate-grey hair and long, wispy beard stream sideways as if in a gale. He wears a huge, billowing cloak made of dark-grey storm clouds, torn into ragged wisps at the edges, and from the knees down he fades into swirling grey mist.

Story world: Old Norway by the sea, long ago. The fisherman's small grey cottage with a turf roof stands on the shore right next to the king's castle, and his boat is a small, tarred, dark-brown rowing boat with two oars. Far across the great sea lies Hvittenland, whose beach is sand as white as milk, with the trolls' gloomy grey castle on a hill behind it and two lions at its gate. The queen's own castle in Hvittenland is white, with a stone stair up to its door. The trolls' birch switches are bundles of thin, bare birch twigs. The queen's wish ring is a plain gold ring, and the little ring she ties into his hair is a tiny gold ring on a blue thread. The magic hat, cloak and boots are a tall grey felt hat, a long dark-grey hooded cloak and a pair of tall brown boots.

This story's season, light and colours: The bright, cold light of early spring in the far north: a copper-red sunset over the sea at the start, then the dazzling milk-white beach of Hvittenland under a pale pearl-blue sky, with turquoise shallows and pale lemon sunrises. The tickling nights happen in near darkness, lit by one warm candle. On the long journey: deep snow still on blue mountains, a steel-grey cold sea and wild, racing storm clouds. Accents: the princess's sky blue and the gold of rings and crowns.

Bog cotton grows in fluffy white tufts, and everything made from it is soft and snow-white. The old gardener is small and bald with a grey beard; his wife is tall and thin in a white headscarf. The three children are two boys with fair curls and a girl with black hair.

Snehvit og Rosenrød snehvit-og-rosenrod · the Maiden

Den stille, snille prinsessen som vandrer ut i verden for å gjøre godt igjen og redde sine tolv brødre ved å arbeide tålmodig og modig.

A slim girl of about seventeen with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large, dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder, tied with a white ribbon. She wears a plain dark-teal wool dress with a deep front pocket, where the handle of a small silver spoon peeks out, a long grey knitted shawl and thin, worn brown shoes.

Snehvit og Rosenrød som dronning snehvit-og-rosenrod-dronning · the Maiden Queen

Prinsessen etter at hun har giftet seg med den unge kongen. Om kveldene syr hun skjorter av myrull, og hun kan ikke si et ord, selv når stemoren lyver om henne.

A slim young woman of about eighteen with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large, dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder, under a slender silver crown. She wears a long, simple gown of snow-white linen embroidered with small rose-red roses along the hem and cuffs, a rose-red sash and soft grey slippers.

Dronningen dronningen · the Queen

Moren til de tolv prinsene og prinsessen. Hun ønsket seg en datter så hvit som snø og så rød som blod, og så mistet hun de tolv guttene sine.

A warm, motherly queen of about forty with a round face, a soft double chin, a small snub nose, kind hazel eyes, rosy cheeks and wavy chestnut hair going grey at the temples, pinned up under a small gold crown. She wears a long plum-purple winter cloak lined and trimmed with thick white fur over a plum gown, white fur mittens and fur-lined boots.

Trollkjerringen trollkjerringen · the Troll Hag

En gammel trollkjerring med nese som en potet og hår som et kråkereir, som gjør de tolv prinsene om til villender.

A short, stout old troll woman, no taller than a fence, with lumpy, sandy-beige skin, a huge knobbly nose exactly like a big potato, small beady black eyes, a wide crooked grin with three teeth, and an enormous tangle of black-and-grey hair like a crow's nest, stuck with twigs and one black feather. A thin cow's tail with a tuft pokes out under her patched grey skirt, and she wears a ragged moss-green shawl and big grey felt boots.

Den unge kongen den-unge-kongen · the Young King

En godhjertet konge som møter prinsessen på myra, tar vare på henne og søker sannheten når det oppstår mistanke.

A tall, slim young king of about twenty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, friendly face, a straight nose, warm brown eyes, a wide smile and fair, straight hair tied back at the neck with a dark-blue ribbon. On his head sits a thin gold circlet. He wears a sky-blue wool coat trimmed with white braid and fastened with brass toggles, a broad brown leather belt, fawn trousers, soft grey suede boots and a short grey travelling cloak.

Den gamle stemoren den-gamle-stemoren · the Old Stepmother

En misunnelig, lur kvinne ved slottet som skaper uro med løgner, men til slutt blir sendt bort så hun ikke kan skade noen.

A bony, very upright old woman with a long, pointed chin, a small hooked nose, narrow darting eyes, thin lips, a heavily powdered white face with two round spots of pink rouge, and a tall tower of steel-grey hair stuck with jewelled pins. She wears a stiff black brocade gown shot with silver thread and a tall, fan-shaped collar of grey lace, rings on every finger, and a silver hand mirror on a chain at her waist.

Den yngste broren den-yngste-broren · the Youngest Brother

Den yngste av de tolv brødrene som er villender om dagen og prinser om natten. Han er snill mot søsteren sin fra første stund.

A slim young man of about sixteen, the smallest of twelve brothers, with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a faded bottle-green cap, a worn chestnut-brown wool tunic with a white collar and a rope belt, patched grey trousers and soft grey boots.

Den yngste broren med vingen den-yngste-broren-vinge · the Winged Brother

Den yngste broren når trolldommen er brutt. Den siste skjorten fikk bare ett erme, så han har en andevinge i stedet for venstre arm.

He wears a new, soft snow-white shirt, cap and scarf woven from bog cotton, grey trousers and soft grey boots. The three children are two boys with fair curls and a girl with black hair.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Twelve princes on twelve horses ride in through the archway of the Castle Courtyard, all in new snow-white shirts, caps and scarves. In front rides the Winged Brother, a big grey-brown duck wing where his left arm should be, waving happily with his right hand. The Maiden Queen presses both hands to her heart, and the Young King stares in wonder. Morning sun on the cobbles.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Winged Brother: A slim young man of about sixteen with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a new, soft snow-white shirt, cap and scarf woven from bog cotton, grey trousers and soft grey boots. In place of his left arm he has a large wild duck's wing of grey-brown feathers with a shiny blue-violet patch edged in white.
- the Maiden Queen: A slim young woman of about eighteen with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large, dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder, under a slender silver crown. She wears a long, simple gown of snow-white linen embroidered with small rose-red roses along the hem and cuffs, a rose-red sash and soft grey slippers.
- the Young King: A tall, slim young king of about twenty-five, clean-shaven, with a long, friendly face, a straight nose, warm brown eyes, a wide smile and fair, straight hair tied back at the neck with a dark-blue ribbon. On his head sits a thin gold circlet. Setting:
- the Castle Courtyard: A wide cobbled courtyard in front of the young king's castle, a long, dark-red painted timber castle with white window frames, a tall gate tower with a shingled spire and a broad wooden stair up to the main door. A round stone well stands in the middle, and a wide archway in the far wall opens onto a bumpy road leading into the spruce forest.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The queen's castle lies among wide, snowy fields, with a grey split-rail fence along the sleigh road; her sleigh is small and red with brass bells, pulled by one brown horse. The thirteen silver spoons are alike, each with a tiny crown on the handle. As wild ducks, the twelve brothers are mallard drakes with glossy bottle-green heads, white neck rings, chestnut breasts and grey backs. As men they look alike, with tousled raven-black hair, bottle-green caps and chestnut-brown tunics; the eldest is the tallest and has a short black beard. Bog cotton grows in fluffy white tufts, and everything made from it is soft and snow-white. The old gardener is small and bald with a grey beard; his wife is tall and thin in a white headscarf. The three children are two boys with fair curls and a girl with black hair.

This story's season, light and colours: Snow-white, rose-red and raven-black accents throughout. Night in the candlelit Little Chamber. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a huge, hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise. The door has creaked open, and three curious old faces peek in around it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking in first, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway. Rain streaks the window.

Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: Night in the candlelit Little Chamber. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a huge, hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise. The door has creaked open, and three curious old faces peek in around it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking in first, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway. Rain streaks the window.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about sixteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and an enormous nose as long and thick as a cucumber, poking far out in front of her face with a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green shawl with a fringe, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and huge round eyes as big as saucers, pink-rimmed and always brimming with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously wide hips, so wide that her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.

Setting:
- the Little Chamber: A small, cosy room at the royal farm with honey-brown log walls and a low, beamed ceiling. A narrow wooden bed with a thick white duvet stands against one wall. A small table sits under a four-paned window with rain running down the glass, a wooden spinning wheel stands beside it, and a big upright wooden loom fills the far corner. A candle holder on the table, a striped rag rug on the floor and a plank door with an iron latch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. A poor hunter lives in a small log cabin deep in a spruce forest. The royal farm is a big, friendly cluster of honey-brown log buildings with grass roofs, carved gables and small-paned windows around a cobbled yard with a well. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a big wicker basket; spun, it becomes smooth, shiny golden yarn wound into soft balls; woven, it becomes a thick roll of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a neat pile of white linen shirts with shiny buttons. The Queen's servant girls are three young women in grey dresses, white aprons and white caps. The wedding is held in the royal farm's great hall, with six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long rainy spell at the end of summer: silver rain streaming down small-paned windows, dripping gardens in deep, wet greens and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sunshine sparkling on puddles and wet leaves. Indoors: warm candle and lamp light on flax-gold yarn, cream linen and soft wool colours. The wedding glows with candlelight, bowls of pink and white garden flowers and a tall cake. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

Characters

Jenta jenta · the Girl

En snill og modig jente som vil klare seg selv, men som også lærer at det er lov å ta imot hjelp.

A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about sixteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.

Bruden bruden · the Bride

Jenta på bryllupsdagen sin, med blomsterkrans og brudekjole. Nå skjønner hun hvilken stor dag mostrene mente.

The Girl on her wedding day: the same slim girl of about sixteen with an oval, freckled face, a snub nose, big hazel eyes and a wide smile, her mousy-brown hair now brushed out long and wavy over her shoulders under a wreath of pink and white roses and green myrtle. She wears a flowing cream-white linen wedding dress with lace at the square neckline and cuffs, a pale-green silk sash tied in a big bow, and the blue jay feather tucked into the wreath.

Dronningen dronningen · the Queen

En håndarbeidsglad dronning som setter pris på det som er vakkert laget, og som til slutt viser omsorg og godhet.

A tall, willowy, kindly queen of about fifty with a long neck, a long oval face, crinkly grey eyes, a slightly long nose and dark hair streaked with silver in a low, coiled knot under a small gold crown. She wears a sea-green gown with a frilled cream collar and a long rainbow-striped knitted shawl, and she is always knitting with two long wooden needles, a half-finished striped scarf and a ball of pink yarn.

Prinsen prinsen · the Prince

En høflig og nysgjerrig prins som forstår at kjærlighet også handler om å ta vare på hverandre.

A tall, slender, polite young prince of about nineteen with a long, clean-shaven face, a dimpled chin, a long nose with a little bump, earnest dark eyes under thick eyebrows and short, tidy black curls. He wears a small silver crown, a deep-teal velvet jacket with a row of silver buttons, a ruffled cream shirt, charcoal breeches and tall tan riding boots.

Mosteren med den lange nesa moster-langnese · the Long-Nosed Aunt

Den første mosteren, som spinner alt linet for jenta om natta. Nesa har blitt så lang av all nikkingen ved rokken.

A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and an enormous nose as long and thick as a cucumber, poking far out in front of her face with a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green shawl with a fringe, and leans on a crooked walking stick.

Mosteren som er bred bak moster-bred · the Broad-Hipped Aunt

Den andre mosteren, som vever alt garnet til tøy. Hun har sittet så lenge på vevbenken at hun er blitt bred som et høylass bak.

A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously wide hips, so wide that her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.

Mosteren med de røde øynene moster-roede-oyne · the Teary-Eyed Aunt

Den tredje mosteren, som syr skjortene med bitte små sting natt og dag, så øynene hennes er blitt store, røde og rennende.

A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and huge round eyes as big as saucers, pink-rimmed and always brimming with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.

- the Prince: A tall, slender, polite young prince of about nineteen with a long, clean-shaven face, a dimpled chin, a long nose with a little bump, earnest dark eyes under thick eyebrows and short, tidy black curls. He wears a small silver crown, a deep-teal velvet jacket with a row of silver buttons, a ruffled cream shirt, charcoal breeches and tall tan riding boots.
- the Queen: A tall, willowy, kindly queen of about fifty with a long neck, a long oval face, crinkly grey eyes, a slightly long nose and dark hair streaked with silver in a low, coiled knot under a small gold crown. She wears a sea-green gown with a frilled cream collar and a long rainbow-striped knitted shawl, and she is always knitting with two long wooden needles, a half-finished striped scarf and a ball of pink yarn.

Setting:
- the Great Hall: A long, warm hall of dark timber with a high ceiling and red-and-green rosemaling on the carved beams, lit by candles in iron chandeliers. Down the middle runs a long table covered with a white linen cloth and set with bowls of pink and white garden flowers, tall candles, plates and a tall, cream-covered cake, with carved wooden chairs along both sides. At one end stands a tall, carved double door.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. A poor hunter lives in a small log cabin deep in a spruce forest. The royal farm is a big, friendly cluster of honey-brown log buildings with grass roofs, carved gables and small-paned windows around a cobbled yard with a well. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a big wicker basket; spun, it becomes smooth, shiny golden yarn wound into soft balls; woven, it becomes a thick roll of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a neat pile of white linen shirts with shiny buttons. The Queen's servant girls are three young women in grey dresses, white aprons and white caps. The wedding is held in the royal farm's great hall, with six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long rainy spell at the end of summer: silver rain streaming down small-paned windows, dripping gardens in deep, wet greens and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sunshine sparkling on puddles and wet leaves. Indoors: warm candle and lamp light on flax-gold yarn, cream linen and soft wool colours. The wedding glows with candlelight, bowls of pink and white garden flowers and a tall cake. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Characters

Vesle Aase vesle-aase · Vesle Aase

En snill og rolig gåsepike som passer kongens gjess og tør å være ærlig, selv når andre prøver å skjule sannheten.

A small, sturdy goose girl of about fifteen, a head shorter than most, with a round, sun-browned face, a small determined chin, a snub nose, calm dark-brown eyes that look straight at you and thick, straight eyebrows. Her thick dark-brown hair is in one short, stubby plait tied with red wool. She wears a plain brown wool dress mended with neat blue and green patches, a crisp white apron, wooden clogs and a little patchwork sewing bag hanging from her apron string.

Vesle Aase som brud vesle-aase-brud · Vesle Aase the Bride

Vesle Aase på bryllupsdagen, i en ny kjole uten en eneste lapp og med ringen til kongssønnen på fingeren.

A small, sturdy girl of about fifteen, a head shorter than most, with a round, sun-browned face, a small determined chin, a snub nose, calm dark-brown eyes and thick, straight eyebrows. Her thick dark-brown hair is pinned up under a small, glittering silver bridal crown with dangling spangles. She wears a new buttercup-yellow wedding dress without a single patch, embroidered with white daisies around the hem, soft white shoes and a slim gold ring with a tiny red stone on one finger.

Kongssønnen fra England kongssonnen-fra-england · the Prince

En høflig prins som leter etter den snilleste og mest ærlige han kan gifte seg med, og som velger å handle rolig når han blir skuffet.

A tall, lean prince of about twenty-two with a long, kind face, a slightly long straight nose, calm hazel eyes, neat sandy hair parted at the side and a small, neatly trimmed sandy moustache. He wears a small gold crown, a bright scarlet riding coat with gold frogging across the chest, a white cravat, cream trousers and brown top boots with turned-down cuffs, and he has a polite, patient smile.

Sannhetssteinen sannhetssteinen · the Truth Stone

En liten blank stein som avslører om noen prøver å lure, og som hjelper prinsen å forstå hvem som er ærlig.

A small, smooth, egg-shaped stone no bigger than a plum, polished so shiny that it gleams like a pearl: milky white with faint swirls of pale gold and rose inside. It has no face, but when it speaks or someone steps over it, it glows with a soft, warm golden light that spreads around it like candlelight. It lies quite still, looking wise and quietly magical.

Den tredje prinsessa den-tredje-prinsessa · the Third Princess

En vakker prinsesse som blir urolig for at sannheten skal komme fram, og derfor prøver å bytte plass med Aase om natta.

A tall, willowy princess of about eighteen with a long neck, a narrow face, high arched brows over big, anxious dark-brown eyes, a delicate little mouth and glossy chocolate-brown hair in long, bouncy ringlets tied back with a pearl-studded ribbon. She wears a small pearl tiara, pearl earrings and a long peacock-blue gown with puffed sleeves and a lace collar, and carries a large white feather fan that she likes to hide behind.
