In the front row of wooden benches sit eight geese, white and grey, big and small, very proud and upright. Behind them ten smiling guests in their finest clothes clap their hands. Sunlight streams in through tall windows.

Full prompt
Reference images:
- Image 1: model sheet for Vesle Aase the Bride, the same character seen from three sides. Keep Vesle Aase the Bride's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw Vesle Aase the Bride only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 2: model sheet for the Prince, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Prince's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Prince only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: A festive castle hall decorated with birch branches and spring flowers. Vesle Aase the Bride and the Prince stand hand in hand at the front, beaming. In the front row of wooden benches sit eight geese, white and grey, big and small, very proud and upright. Behind them ten smiling guests in their finest clothes clap their hands. Sunlight streams in through tall windows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Vesle Aase the Bride: A small, sturdy girl of about fifteen, a head shorter than most, with a round, sun-browned face, a small determined chin, a snub nose, calm dark-brown eyes and thick, straight eyebrows. Her thick dark-brown hair is pinned up under a small, glittering silver bridal crown with dangling spangles. She wears a new buttercup-yellow wedding dress without a single patch, embroidered with white daisies around the hem, soft white shoes and a slim gold ring with a tiny red stone on one finger.
- the Prince: A tall, lean prince of about twenty-two with a long, kind face, a slightly long straight nose, calm hazel eyes, neat sandy hair parted at the side and a small, neatly trimmed sandy moustache. He wears a small gold crown, a bright scarlet riding coat with gold frogging across the chest, a white cravat, cream trousers and brown top boots with turned-down cuffs, and he has a polite, patient smile.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The king's castle is a big, white-painted timber palace with carved wooden balconies and blue window frames, set among green meadows beside a dusty country road with grassy ditches. The king has a large flock of geese, big and small, white and grey. Vesle Aase is always sewing a small dress made of patch on patch in many colours. The fine bedchamber has a tall door painted with blue and red rosemaling flowers and a worn wooden threshold, where the truth stone lies at night. The Prince rides a tall bay horse and wears a slim gold ring with a tiny red stone on his little finger, until the night he slips it onto a sleeping girl's finger.

This story's season, light and colours: Late spring in fresh, gentle pastels: bright-green meadows full of golden dandelions and fluffy white dandelion clocks, white and grey geese, a soft sky-blue sky and clear, milky morning light. The night scenes inside the castle are a deep, hushed blue, lit only by a single candle or the truth stone's warm golden glow.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
